about: Summaries of the conversation in each FOCUS_Spec issue and pull request in the Data model's history that has three or more comments or reviews, written by Claude (an AI model) from each thread as it stood on 2026-11-11. They paraphrase the discussion and name participants by GitHub username.

summaries.42: udam-f2 opened this PR adding the ResourceId column specification and supporting notes for #5. Review was mostly editorial: flanakin suggested wording, asked whether to adopt a style guide, preferred "provider" to "vendor" and proposed moving action items into issues. udam-f2 said the supporting notes were meant to show the discussion behind the column, not spec text, and that the folder structure would evolve. It merged in May 2023.
summaries.49: Pull request #49, by flanakin, added the specification for the ChargeType column and closed #8. Review was mostly editorial: udam-f2 raised how to present allowed values for this first normalized column, whether to use display names, and table formatting, and flanakin moved the value descriptions into content constraints. mike-finopsorg warned that 'MUST contain' could be misread as substring matching. udam-f2 approved and it merged in May 2023.
summaries.65: ijurica submitted the Invoicing Entity spec changes for #31, renaming the dimension to Invoice Issuer and replacing "infrastructure" wording with "resources". Open points carried over from the Provider discussion in #11 included whether normative text should use column IDs or display names. mike-finopsorg asked whether a link would work in the PDF; udam-f2 said an anchor was needed. udam-f2 approved, and it was merged in May 2023.
summaries.96: MichaelArkoosh-vega proposed the SubAccountName column specification. rileyjenk requested changes, noting that sub accounts can generate invoices, so MichaelArkoosh-vega suggested saying instead that sub accounts do not receive invoices; udam-f2 agreed after checking the MSP case. The wording was updated accordingly, alongside formatting suggestions from flanakin and ijurica, and the PR was merged in June 2023.
summaries.99: amitw-g proposed the BillingAccountId dimension for #17. rileyjenk raised a conflict with sub-accounts that receive their own invoices, citing AWS payer and linked accounts. udam-f2 noted a billing account is what gets invoiced and opened a new issue for the higher-level grouping that rileyjenk and ijurica wanted. Other review was wording, including removing a Google Docs link, and it merged in June 2023.
summaries.100: Pull request #100, by chandra-cloudtrakr, created a Billed Cost metric for #38. flanakin and udam-f2 proposed wording that billed cost includes negotiated discounts but does not amortize up-front charges. flanakin asked whether organizations use amortized cost for allocation, and udam-f2 replied only when a central team pays the up-front cost. udam-f2 approved and it merged in June 2023.
summaries.104: In June 2023 flanakin proposed requiring consistent casing for provider-specified column values, since "brazil" and "Brazil" would group separately. In January 2024 udam-f2 asked whether it was still relevant, and flanakin called it a minor item to either fix or close. In February 2024 ijurica reported TF-1 preferred one global attribute requiring consistent value formats instead of per-column rules. No comment records the outcome; GitHub shows it closed as completed.
summaries.111: dingy999 proposed adding an Availability Zone dimension (issue #93). mikepolson-vmware asked whether it held one value or several and suggested making it optional, as did flanakin; dingy999 said it was single-valued, with multiple zones as separate rows. rileyjenk noted AWS zone names differ between customers, and dingy999 said v0.5 passed provider values through, leaving normalization for later. It merged in June 2023.
summaries.116: flanakin proposed rewording the ServiceName definition to be more explicit about what the value represents. udam-f2 and amitw-g asked whether it should be called a display name, like other name columns; flanakin agreed for consistency, though no matching ID existed. udam-f2 suggested rewordings, including describing an offering that "encapsulates resources and/or services", which flanakin felt added ambiguity. The pull request was merged in June 2023.
summaries.117: SanjnaSrivatsaVMware proposed the BillingCurrency column for #92. Review was mostly editorial: udam-f2 asked for proper headings, separate supporting content and a reference to the Currency Code Format attribute rather than the ISO standard, while rodneyjoyce and rupagcp suggested simpler wording and consistent Google Cloud naming. mikepolson-vmware and udam-f2 approved, and it merged in June 2023.
summaries.118: flanakin added the ServiceCategory column. chandra-cloudtrakr asked for a statement that it MUST be a String, which flanakin added to match the currency code column. rodneyjoyce asked what "restricted" meant (flanakin said normalized) and asked for consistent capitalization, while ijurica questioned the Azure mapping, which flanakin said should be ServiceFamily. mikepolson-vmware and udam-f2 approved, and it merged in June 2023.
summaries.121: Pull request #121, by SanjnaSrivatsaVMware, created the Billing Period End column for #107. amitw-g suggested wording, and udam-f2 noted that columns are referred to by display name. flanakin asked whether to clarify that the exclusive end value is really the start of the next period; udam-f2 argued it is semantically the end because it is exclusive. It merged in June 2023.
summaries.122: rileyjenk opened this PR to add an Amortized Cost metric with supporting content, covering how upfront and recurring commitment fees are spread across usage. flanakin asked to generalise reservation-specific wording and noted that Microsoft did not report data the way the examples assumed, while kk09v fixed the amortization formula and terminology. MichaelArkoosh-vega queried text about organisations using other amortization approaches, and rileyjenk said the group had settled on the provider's method. udam-f2 proposed dropping a non-normative statement that amortized totals would not match the invoice, and suggested providers distribute commitment purchases rather than show an upfront line, which flanakin wanted stated more directly. flanakin felt one passage lacked specificity but was acceptable for 0.5. rodneyjoyce questioned relying on Google Sheets examples. udam-f2 approved, and it merged in June 2023.
summaries.123: ijurica proposed a Date/Time attribute requiring date and time columns to use UTC and ISO 8601 formatting. jasonkellyAP doubted providers would adopt the format, so ijurica softened the provider expectations; flanakin offered wording edits and asked whether seconds should be optional, and ijurica replied that the squad had agreed to keep second-level precision only. rodneyjoyce said it looked good, udam-f2 approved, and it was merged in June 2023.
summaries.144: rileyjenk proposed renaming the Amortized Cost metric to Effective Cost because of extensive feedback about the name. flanakin requested changes, asking that the supporting content be updated too, and rileyjenk added the supporting docs. udam-f2 approved, and the PR was merged in September 2023.
summaries.166: flowerinthenight proposed a column identifying commitment-based discounts, closing #149. flanakin asked for it to be renamed Commitment Discount ID, to allow nulls for unrelated charges and to avoid wording that implied a GUID. rileyjenk requested changes, arguing that dropping "discount" from the name would also cover on-demand capacity reservations; aqu-erp disagreed, since such reservations have no term and their costs are driven by the instance, and flanakin said the two can overlap, so capacity reservations would get a separate backlog column, which rileyjenk accepted. udam-f2, aqu-erp and marc-perreaut debated the definition of a commitment-based discount, its main uses such as chargeback, and whether to say charge or record. caseydoran approved, and the PR was merged in October 2023.
summaries.167: flowerinthenight's pull request added the CommitmentDiscountName column, closing #150, and was renamed from CommitmentName during review. flanakin, rodneyjoyce and marc-perreaut suggested wording changes, such as not saying who assigns the name and not banning duplication of the ID. rileyjenk argued for dropping "discount" so commitments like capacity reservations would fit; that review was dismissed. It merged in October 2023.
summaries.168: SanjnaSrivatsaVMware opened this pull request for #154 to add a Charge Frequency dimension describing how often a charge occurs. Much of the debate was about value names: flanakin suggested Recurring instead of Periodic, and caseydoran requested changes for the same reason, noting the three major cloud providers used that word. rodneyjoyce, udam-f2 and hekike questioned whether Usage-Based was really a frequency, hekike noting usage can also be billed monthly; flanakin explained it meant charges recur with usage. udam-f2 raised all-upfront reservations, which SanjnaSrivatsaVMware treated as One-Time. flanakin added editorial fixes and a table of charge type and frequency combinations, excluding Purchase with Usage-Based. udam-f2 approved and it was merged in October 2023; afterwards rupagcp questioned whether Recurring suited tax charges.
summaries.171: cnharris10 proposed a Resource Type column (issue #172). flanakin asked whether values should be human-readable names or provider identifiers such as Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines; cnharris10 did not want to limit it to readable text, and udam-f2 wanted guidance on values. udam-f2 also objected to nonstandard sections and examples in normative content, and proposed that ResourceType be non-null whenever ResourceId is. It merged in October 2023.
summaries.173: For #151, rodneyjoyce drafted a column, written as CommitmentDiscountType, saying whether a commitment discount was spend-based or usage-based. udam-f2 pushed for a tighter definition distinct from negotiated discounts, provider mappings and a note on why it was commitment-specific; flanakin questioned "spend" as jargon and suggested tying nullability to CommitmentDiscountId. On value names, flanakin questioned the -Based suffix, which marc-perreaut found superfluous, and ljadvey proposed plain Spend and Usage, while udam-f2 preferred more descriptive terms. TDubovchenko and yprikhodko noted Savings Plans had been misclassified, which rodneyjoyce fixed, and cnharris10 asked to keep capacity reservations out. shawnalpay asked about telling novices that Reservations are usage-based and Savings Plans spend-based; udam-f2 objected that this reflected provider naming, not a generic concept. jasonkellyAP, flowerinthenight and udam-f2 approved, and it was merged in November 2023.
summaries.179: JGrubb opened this PR to define a Pricing Unit dimension (issue #169). Reviewers went through many rewrites of the definition: flanakin objected to the word "basis" as jargon, and udam-f2 asked whether a recommended unit list was needed, as for Usage Unit. In November 2023 the group renamed the column PricingMeasure and left it non-normalized. shawnalpay went on record against the name, saying "Measure" means something else in reporting models, and rileyjenk warned the rename would confuse. Days later the group reversed course and chose a semi-normalized Pricing Unit that follows the Unit Format attribute, like Usage Unit. flanakin asked for a separate PricingBlockSize, which udam-f2 proposed as a fast follow in v1.x. The PR merged on 13 November 2023.
summaries.186: MichaelArkoosh-vega proposed a usage quantity column for #182. The name shifted from amitw-g's QuantityInUsageUnit to UsageQuantity after flanakin argued it should sit beside PricingQuantity. Reviewers fixed contradictory nullability wording, tobrien clarified that it measured usage rather than pricing, and ghost requested changes to use a non-normalized PricingMeasure. udam-f2 approved, and it merged in November 2023.
summaries.214: rodneyjoyce opened this PR from a 0.5 draft of a column first written as PricingModel and merged as Pricing Category (issue #161), with flanakin drafting much of the text. The values were contested. marc-perreaut and flanakin questioned how Fixed differed from On-Demand. shawnalpay proposed Standard instead of On-Demand, but rodneyjoyce said the VS2 squad preferred On-Demand as better understood. sarahcloudpm saw overlap between Dynamic and On-Demand and asked why Other was needed; mike-finopsorg defended Other as better than null or a wrong value. A Shared value for dedicated hosts, raised by flanakin, was deferred to a point release. udam-f2 argued for a broader Discounted value, which flanakin said grouped too much, and aqu-erp placed finer levels after v1.0. It merged in November 2023.
summaries.221: cnharris10 opened this pull request to add a Charge Description column, closing #220. ljadvey requested changes so the provider mappings named specific columns, as the AWS row did. anatri1 asked whether "Charge" was the right term, since providers used it as a synonym for cost; cnharris10 said that naming debate could happen separately. joshk0 approved and proposed examples of good and bad descriptions, warning against pricing text, marketing copy and opaque SKU codes. flanakin commented without approving, saying the column's purpose and how to fill it were unclear, and asked for such guidance to become MUST or SHOULD requirements. Inline threads also debated nullability, a length limit (cnharris10 said SaaS descriptions can be much longer) and the Azure and GCP mappings. udam-f2 approved, and it was merged in November 2023.
summaries.224: At udam-f2's suggestion, rodneyjoyce changed the ServiceCategory dimension to the format used by all other 0.5 and 1.0 dimensions, though rodneyjoyce preferred the more user-friendly form. flanakin approved for consistency but argued the spec should eventually go the other way. udam-f2 added the broader question to a list of spec-wide consistency changes. It merged in October 2023.
summaries.225: ahullah opened this PR to define a column for the quantity of a resource or service measured in its pricing unit, first named QuantityInPricingUnit. flanakin proposed renaming it PricingQuantity, alongside UsageQuantity, so related columns would sit together, and the PR adopted the new name. joshk0 approved but asked why the column was needed; udam-f2 explained that block pricing makes it differ from usage quantity. Reviewers debated provider mappings: rupagcp and shruthinambi pointed to different Google Cloud fields, and marc-perreaut questioned the Azure mapping, which ijurica left to the converters group. ijurica also questioned requiring credits to be negative, and kk09v noted that unit prices cannot be summed. The PR was merged in November 2023.
summaries.227: cnharris10 opened this pull request to add a Tags column, closing #226, and most discussion happened in inline review threads. ljadvey, mike-finopsorg and others asked what a "finalized" tag meant, and cnharris10 offered alternative wordings; joshk0 favored dropping the terms static, dynamic and finalized altogether. udam-f2 and ljadvey wanted the data type stated as JSON. Reviewers also covered prefixes for provider-defined tags, null values for keys without values (marc-perreaut doubted such tags existed, and cnharris10 pointed to GCP network tags) and whether a survey of provider practice belonged in the spec. marc-perreaut noted that tag inheritance differs by provider. mattray, udam-f2 and shawnalpay approved, joshk0 said they would follow up with tweaks, and it was merged in November 2023.
summaries.233: ijurica revised the BilledCost metric's description and content constraints, adding a list of discounts, and put the metrics in alphabetical order (#232). udam-f2 suggested naming the discounts explicitly rather than grouping them under "all". mattray said it looked good, udam-f2 approved it as mostly wording changes, and it was merged in November 2023.
summaries.234: Pull request #234, by ijurica, revised the ListUnitPrice metric's normative text and provider mapping guidance for #231. nfonrose proposed tying the price to a SkuId, and the definition went through several drafts; after noting that providers also publish commitment-inclusive prices, ijurica removed the SkuPriceId association and stated explicitly which discounts are excluded. yprikhodko questioned whether the column was redundant, since it could be derived from List Cost and usage, and raised spot discounts. flanakin pressed for an explicit warning that prices in billing currency will not match pricing APIs, deferring it to a separate PR. shawnalpay asked that a TODO in supporting content be resolved or struck; ijurica merged anyway, acknowledging the gap. udam-f2 and shawnalpay approved, and it merged in November 2023.
summaries.235: ijurica proposed the List Cost metric for #174. jpickardgreen requested changes, offering a definition that included free-tier and volume-based rates but excluded other discounts and amortization. yprikhodko asked that spot discounts also be excluded so savings from spot could be measured, and ijurica folded that in. flanakin wanted the definition simplified towards a public retail price. shawnalpay asked for the formula to be stated explicitly, and jpickardgreen noted that would need applying to every price-times-quantity metric; shawnalpay also proposed that normative statements start with the keyword. udam-f2 suggested defining it as List Unit Price multiplied by Pricing Quantity, added rules for null prices and approved. It merged in November 2023.
summaries.240: rodneyjoyce proposed a Commitment Discount Type dimension for #241: a provider-assigned name for the type of commitment discount applied. flanakin asked for cloud-specific examples to move to supporting content, and debated with udam-f2 whether the definition should say identify or label. cnharris10 suggested more provider mappings, such as AWS Capacity Blocks and BigQuery Reservations. jasonkellyAP and udam-f2 approved, and it was merged in November 2023.
summaries.244: shawnalpay opened this pull request defining the SKU Price ID column and its supporting content (#243). ijurica asked for a rule that one SkuPriceId cannot relate to more than one SkuId, which shawnalpay added. ijurica later asked how practitioners would find the list unit price when the SKU price already includes commitment discounts, and suggested a future column holding the matching list price ID, while approving. In inline threads the description was reworded on a VS3 working group call; marc-perreaut objected to wording implying a SKU has only one price; udam-f2 asked whether column names should use Sku or SKU; mike-finopsorg proposed tying each SkuPriceId to a single list unit price; and aqu-erp and flanakin refined the OCI, Azure and GCP mappings. It was merged in November 2023.
summaries.248: This mostly editorial pull request by flanakin replaced scattered uses of "record" and "line item" with "row", after flowerinthenight noticed the mixed terms. udam-f2 objected to unrelated auto-formatting changes in the diff. shawnalpay asked whether this meant line item and charge were not synonyms; flanakin said the terms were roughly synonymous and suggested a fuller terminology pass after 1.0. It was merged in November 2023.
summaries.250: ijurica's pull request reviewed the EffectiveCost definition (#249), with related BilledCost wording. rileyjenk objected that Effective Cost is a value, not a charge, so ijurica switched to "cost". Reviewers also refined amortization wording and example tables, and flanakin questioned a sentence saying totals may not match invoices. udam-f2 approved, and it merged in November 2023.
summaries.255: udam-f2 continued arrarama's work from #239 to define the SKU ID column (#242). shruthinambi said GCP's SKU data came from the BigQuery pricing export; udam-f2 replied that the mapping referred to the billing data and added a note about the pricing export. Inline threads set nullability rules tying SkuId to SkuPriceId, and joshk0 asked about refunds. shawnalpay approved, and it was merged in November 2023.
summaries.275: udam-f2 opened this largely editorial PR as a final scrub outside the glossary, moving DataType beside value format, fixing quotes, column types and links, and changing wording such as "cost and usage" to "billing" and "null or empty" to "null". flanakin suggested casing fixes and asked whether price columns are dimensions or metrics; shawnalpay said either view was defensible. It was merged in November 2023.
summaries.280: cnharris10 made minor grammar and formatting fixes to the Tags and Charge Description columns, such as moving from past to present tense and formatting a prefix as code. shawnalpay suggested further wording tweaks, including questioning an "(italicized)" note. The change was purely editorial and merged in November 2023.
summaries.287: flanakin proposed BillingAccountType and SubAccountType columns carrying provider labels for account IDs (for example "Subscription" or "Project"), mirroring ResourceType. TDubovchenko suggested metadata instead; flanakin replied that types vary across billing accounts and providers, so metadata could not describe multi-provider datasets. rupagcp opposed adding them to v1.0 without alignment, and udam-f2 reported in March 2024 that maintainers leaned toward metadata first. ijurica favored mandatory columns, while mlohmeijer, AWS-ZachErdman and rupagcp questioned their practical value and the added schema size. At an April 2024 members meeting some members did not see them as critical for v1.0. Later suggestions from flanakin made them conditional columns introduced in 1.2. Members agreed to the pull request on February 6, 2025, and it merged that month.
summaries.293: ijurica asked in January 2024 whether Pricing Quantity measured the volume of a resource or service or of the SKU, and suggested rewording; the same applied to Usage Quantity. flanakin suggested combining it with #294, and ijurica pointed to #324 for the definition changes and #327 for pricing unit questions. udam-f2 closed it in February 2024 as a duplicate of #294, since one PR handled both.
summaries.294: ijurica asked in January 2024 whether UsageQuantity should describe the volume of a SKU rather than a resource or service, and when it must be null. flanakin agreed it concerned SKU usage, including purchases, while aqu-erp and thecloudman questioned block pricing and how usage and pricing quantities differ. ijurica narrowed the work to definition and nullability in #324, moving unit questions to #327, and reported #324 closed in February 2024.
summaries.296: cnharris10 asked whether FOCUS should cover all billing data, and whether small SaaS vendors must provide every column even when most would be null. kk09v saw IaaS, PaaS and SaaS as in scope, while flanakin, cnharris10 and thecloudman favoured a smaller required core set. In February 2024 udam-f2 listed 16 columns chosen as "FOCUS Essential" and linked #331. The thread doesn't record the final outcome.
summaries.304: flanakin asked in January 2024 whether the Region column should hold a display name, as most columns did, or be split into RegionId and RegionName. mike-finopsorg backed having both to ease joins, while marc-perreaut preferred a single column. In February 2024 cnharris10 reported that maintainers had decided the column was an ID and should be renamed RegionId, with RegionName still to be discussed. ilia-semenov then opened #352.
summaries.314: flanakin opened this in January 2024 because the SkuId definition did not tell providers what value to use, wanting it tied to retail product thinking. ijurica asked which properties belong to the SKU versus the SKU Price; marc-perreaut suggested SKUs represent types of usage. Task forces classified SKU properties through late 2024, with ijurica to draft a clarifying PR. shawnalpay closed it in May 2025, all action items complete.
summaries.317: flanakin proposed BillingAccountType and SubAccountType columns, following the ResourceId and ResourceType pattern, because the entities behind BillingAccountId and SubAccountId vary by provider and agreement. marc-perreaut questioned repeating values that might be constant per provider; flanakin replied that Microsoft agreements differ, and thecloudman saw value in SubAccountType. Members moved it to v1.1 in April 2024; it was reopened in February 2025 and closed with all action items complete in May 2025.
summaries.319: cnharris10 proposed columns showing how much of a commitment was used, such as used and total commitment quantity and a unit. flanakin argued existing columns already gave used amounts, totals needed another dataset, and unused commitment still needed ChargeSubcategory. cnharris10 saw the columns as additive, sparing practitioners the calculation. In May 2024 the maintainers classified it under Discounts; no comment records the outcome, and GitHub shows it closed as completed.
summaries.324: ijurica revised the definitions and normative text of PricingQuantity, PricingUnit, UsageQuantity and UsageUnit for #294. rileyjenk worried that separate pricing and usage units would often hold identical values and might imply they should differ; ijurica deferred that to a separate PR with sample data (#327) and noted that unused commitments and credits should be excluded when reconciling usage. tobrien, jvdwiel and udam-f2 approved, and it was merged in February 2024.
summaries.330: flanakin merged #305, #306 and #308 into one issue on ChargeSubcategory, commitment utilization and pricing categories. thecloudman suggested a CommitmentStatus column and ahullah separated credits from refunds. In April 2024 the group made Credit a ChargeCategory, moved refunds to a new ChargeClass column and commitment status to a CommitmentDiscountUsage column, removed ChargeSubcategory, renamed two pricing categories to Standard and Committed, and deferred PricingSubcategory until after GA, pending #382 and #383.
summaries.331: udam-f2 proposed grading columns by how required they were, first as a "FOCUS Essential" set and, once #372 was merged in, as mandatory, conditional or optional feature levels. flanakin disliked an Essential label and pushed for conditional presence, such as requiring SkuId when a provider has several SKUs; udam-f2 saw Essential as an easy marketing term for a basic requirement set. ijurica proposed adding SkuId to the essentials and mapped references to non-essential columns; marc-perreaut thought PricingUnit and PricingQuantity sufficed and saw no problem when a referenced column was absent. rupagcp doubted Charge Frequency was essential, rileyjenk asked whether ListCost needed a published list price, and flanakin's objection to making AvailabilityZone a MUST moved to #367. cnharris10 and marc-perreaut approved, and members approved it in April 2024.
summaries.336: ijurica asked for a way to calculate savings from negotiation, suggesting NegotiatedUnitPrice and NegotiatedCost columns or a NegotiatedDiscount column. kk09v raised the order in which stacked discounts apply, and flanakin argued for the more inclusive names OnDemandUnitPrice and OnDemandCost, since many organizations have no negotiated discounts. In March 2024 the discussion moved to #364.
summaries.342: AWS-ZachErdman asked whether the rule giving a valueless tag key a null value forced every tag key onto every row. udam-f2 and cnharris10 said it targeted label-only tags, such as GCP network tags. flanakin opposed excluding null-valued key-value tags, so AWS-ZachErdman proposed limiting the rule to keys that cannot hold values, and cnharris10 relayed rileyjenk's idea of using true instead of null. No comment records the outcome; GitHub shows it closed as completed.
summaries.343: AWS-ZachErdman noted in February 2024 that EffectiveCost's reference to all reduced rates left unclear whether tiered rates should be blended, and proposed stating that it excludes blending. flanakin suggested a simple pull request, which became #350. mike-finopsorg explained why AWS blended costs were of limited use and welcomed a future discussion of a BlendedEffectiveCost. The thread doesn't record the outcome of #350.
summaries.349: cnharris10 clarified Tags handling (#342): keys that cannot hold values get a true value, and tags not set on a resource are left out. rileyjenk argued null and missing values differ and providers should choose. AWS-ZachErdman and rupagcp asked for fuller examples, and flanakin sought practitioner agreement on Booleans, getting a small acknowledgment on a call. Members approved it in March 2024 and it merged.
summaries.350: AWS-ZachErdman proposed, for #343, stating explicitly that EffectiveCost does not use blended rates, plus a small grammar fix. flanakin warned that many readers misunderstand "blending", so AWS-ZachErdman offered simpler wording saying Effective Cost does not mix costs across charges of the same service. rileyjenk approved it as reflecting the original intent, and it was merged in March 2024.
summaries.352: ilia-semenov opened this PR to create a Region ID column as part of splitting Region into Region ID and Region Name. cnharris10 questioned a firm MUST because Region was not a FOCUS Essential column, while SanjnaSrivatsaVMware argued a resource's region must be reported; ljadvey proposed requiring the column only when providers offer regional deployment. After the files were renamed, it was approved and merged in March 2024.
summaries.353: SanjnaSrivatsaVMware opened a PR adding a Region Name column, with ljadvey to fill in the supporting content. udam-f2 asked that it reference RegionId rather than duplicate it, cnharris10 proposed conditional presence wording matching #352 and marking it non-essential, and aqu-erp asked about services spanning several regions. mike-finopsorg approved, noting that providers sometimes use region names rather than IDs in APIs. It was merged in March 2024.
summaries.355: ahullah opened this PR for #330 to move refunds and credits out of ChargeCategory into a separate column, so Usage, Purchase and Tax charges could each be marked as regular or a correction. flanakin asked to keep Adjustment in ChargeCategory for rounding errors and unexpected charges, which ahullah restored, and to merge stray supporting content. The new column's name was contested: udam-f2, shawnalpay and flanakin offered alternatives, Transaction Category was floated, and Charge Class was approved on a joint working group call. cnharris10 found "Regular" and "Correction" too abstract. thecloudman doubted the column's value, wanted an adjustment type instead and moved that to a new issue. Later suggestions were left for future issues. udam-f2 approved, and it merged in April 2024.
summaries.364: ijurica's PR, implementing #336, added unit price and cost columns reflecting negotiated discounts, with naming debated among Negotiated, OnDemand and NegotiatedList. After a vote moved away from "Negotiated", the columns became ContractedUnitPrice and ContractedCost; shawnalpay objected that "negotiated discount" is established FinOps parlance and the new term would confuse adopters, while accepting being in the minority. The group approved it on April 4, 2024, and it was merged.
summaries.365: flanakin proposed a changelog appendix, based on a keepachangelog-style template, so differences between versions are clear, plus a PR template requiring changelog updates. jpradocueva proposed a table showing the version each column was introduced and last updated, and projectlocale supported it. flanakin reopened the issue in April 2024 because the changelog was not complete. No comment records the outcome; GitHub shows it closed as completed.
summaries.366: Issue #366, opened by ahullah from a discussion on #331, asked what List, Contracted, Billed and Effective Cost should hold when a provider has no published price list; rileyjenk had worried that requiring list cost would deter vendors. In April 2024 TF-1 agreed to raise a PR reviewing SkuPriceId and the price, cost and quantity columns after the ChargeCategory cleanup. No comment records the outcome; GitHub shows it closed as completed.
summaries.382: flanakin's PR, for #330, added a column showing whether a commitment discount portion was used or unused. AWS-ZachErdman asked why not use ChargeCategory values instead; flanakin said practitioners wanted unused amounts included when filtering on "Usage". Members agreed the content on April 11, 2024, pending a naming poll among options such as CommitmentDiscountUsage and Commitment Status. The group chose CommitmentDiscountStatus and approved it on April 18, and it was merged.
summaries.383: flanakin's PR carried out decisions from #330, renaming the PricingCategory values On-Demand to Standard and Commitment-Based to Committed, with minor bullet formatting changes. marc-perreaut approved, the member group approved the content in April 2024, and it merged that month.
summaries.396: ijurica added a string attribute, first called StringFormat and later String Handling, and removed value-format consistency rules from four columns (#104). Inline threads covered rules for mutable and immutable strings; cnharris10 doubted providers could always follow them, and udam-f2 preferred keeping MUST with stated exceptions. ijurica worried that null-handling rules clashed with leaving empty strings unaddressed. The group approved it on April 18, 2024, and it was merged that month.
summaries.397: Issue #397, opened by AWS-ZachErdman in April 2024, asked how FOCUS should show whether On-Demand Capacity Reservation usage was used or unused, noting a savings plan could apply to the same line. gparker-at-sf took it on, and AWS-ZachErdman's #509 and ahullah's #515 were deprecated in favour of #523, which proposed ID and Status columns. shawnalpay added a community use case in November 2024. No comment records the outcome; GitHub shows it closed as completed.
summaries.398: cnharris10 proposed, for #380, stating that BillingPeriodStart and ChargePeriodStart are inclusive and the matching End columns exclusive. At the weekly meeting, members including mike-finopsorg asked what inclusive and exclusive meant, prompting glossary entries and examples. projectlocale requested changes over ambiguous sentences and suggested interval notation, and udam-f2 raised formatting points. The group approved it on April 25, 2024, and it was merged that month.
summaries.400: For #319, cnharris10 and ijurica proposed columns tracking commitment discount consumption in the commitment's own units, which often differ from resource units, such as normalized hours or currency. The PR also made ConsumedQuantity and ConsumedUnit null on unused commitment rows. After a hold in mid-2024, thecloudman feared redundant columns bloating datasets and AWS-ZachErdman wanted stronger justification; cnharris10 pointed to the differing units. ijurica and cnharris10 agreed list and contracted costs should be zero for unused commitments. When approval failed in late August, with timwright2000 objecting, separate consumed and purchased quantity columns were merged into one, CommitmentDiscountQuantity, which ijurica endorsed. rileyjenk argued normalization should wait for v1.2 because it only fitted compute; ijurica suggested moving size-flexibility detail into supporting content. Members approved it in September 2024 and it was merged.
summaries.402: Pull request #402, by flanakin, replaced references to ChargeSubcategory across the specification after ChargeClass was introduced (#330). Review was largely mechanical: udam-f2 found leftover ChargeSubcategory mentions, flanakin updated constraint tables to use Feature level, and ijurica asked for the ChargeCategory description and the grouping constructs appendix to be updated too. A PricingQuantity suggestion from aqu-erp was moved to a separate PR after a TF-1 discussion on #366. thecloudman approved and proposed renaming ChargeClass's 'Regular' value to 'Standard' in a separate PR, #410, which ahullah replied had been approved. The group approved #402 on 18 April 2024, though udam-f2 asked that open conversations be resolved first, and it merged in April 2024.
summaries.404: udam-f2 asked in April 2024 for subcategories under ServiceCategory, such as splitting Database into data warehouse, relational and NoSQL. thecloudman agreed but warned against duplicating other columns, suggesting SKU description and resource subtype columns modelled on Azure meter fields. A task force began drafting subcategory principles and a draft list in mid-2024, planning changes after 1.1 to avoid breaking changes. No comment records the outcome; GitHub shows it closed as completed.
summaries.410: thecloudman proposed renaming the ChargeClass value "Regular" to "Standard", matching an earlier change to pricing category values. ahullah and flanakin saw it as an improvement, but udam-f2 relayed marc-perreaut's task force suggestion of "Original", and marc-perreaut also floated renaming the column ChargeOccurrence. ahullah merged it in April 2024, then said that was too soon and opened #422 to change the value to "Original".
summaries.413: ijurica reworked SkuId, SkuPriceId and the price, cost and quantity columns for #366 after the ChargeCategory and ChargeClass cleanup, using a table of when values must be per SKU or may be null. flanakin suggested wording for several columns. Members approved it on April 25, 2024, with a final MAY lowered to "may" and a changelog entry added. It merged in April 2024.
summaries.418: aqu-erp proposed, as one of two paths for #409, limiting UsageQuantity and UsageUnit to usage charges and renaming them ConsumedQuantity and ConsumedUnit, leaving purchase quantities for later. AWS-ZachErdman, udam-f2 and thecloudman preferred this path; marc-perreaut wanted a broader column with a better name, such as StandardizedPricingQuantity. udam-f2 replied that purchase quantities would be handled after v1.0. The group approved it in May 2024.
summaries.428: udam-f2 updated the List Cost and Contracted Cost descriptions to say which purchase charges to exclude to avoid double counting in savings calculations (#424). AWS-ZachErdman suggested clearer wording. flanakin argued that required filtering needed a prescriptive method and asked to avoid "billed basis" jargon; UdamDewaraja defended these as industry terms. The group approved it, planning a follow-up item for remaining concerns, and it was merged in May 2024.
summaries.431: Pull request #431, by ijurica, changed the EffectiveCost definition to cover purchases paid in advance of future eligible charges (#430). thecloudman asked whether it meant amortizing such purchases while excluding the up-front charge, and AWS-ZachErdman and kk09v both saw the wording as a clarification rather than an exception. flanakin approved but found it hard to follow. Members agreed it on 2 May 2024 and it merged that month.
summaries.432: ijurica revised ChargeClass so that "Correction" covered charges invoiced in earlier billing periods, with null otherwise, and adjusted nine related columns (#425). flanakin pointed out that corrections within the same billing period also needed handling, which ijurica accepted, then proposed further values in #435. thecloudman requested a wording change. The group approved it on May 9, 2024, and it was merged that month.
summaries.433: kotzenjh's PR, from consistency review item #426, updated the ChargeCategory definition because parts no longer applied after Credit became its own category and new columns were added. flanakin asked to keep a "commonly used" sentence for consistency, and udam-f2 suggested simpler wording. The group agreed it on May 2, 2024, thecloudman approved, and it was merged that month.
summaries.442: aqu-erp proposed, based on #441, clarifying ChargePeriodStart and ChargePeriodEnd so they match the boundaries of a charge's effective period, covering usage, time-bound purchases and purchases with no end date. udam-f2 asked whether the glossary and a generic End statement needed updating, and AWS-ZachErdman suggested "incurred" wording and dropping the purchase-specific clause. The group approved it on May 9, 2024, and it was merged that day.
summaries.474: aqu-erp proposed, resolving #472, adopting "FOCUS Dataset" as the single term for a dataset meeting FOCUS compliance criteria, defining it in the glossary and using it instead of billing data or cost data in normative statements. ijurica asked whether custom columns must also be listed in the schema metadata and how to write glossary anchors. Maintainers approved it on August 1, 2024, and it was merged that month.
summaries.483: Pull request #483, by AWS-ZachErdman, was an editorial fix correcting the wrong word at the start of the Billing Period End definition. The group agreed it on its 13 June 2024 call and it merged that month.
summaries.495: jpradocueva opened this in July 2024 to track an action item to align SKU properties across providers. AWS-ZachErdman shared a working document and asked other providers which columns distinguish their SKUs and SKU price IDs. Task force and maintainer calls assigned work to gather example data, map provider columns and define common attributes. In August 2024 AWS-ZachErdman linked #516; no comment records the outcome, and GitHub shows it closed as completed.
summaries.503: kk09v opened this PR to add two key-value columns, SkuDetails and SkuPriceDetails, describing properties of a SKU and of a SKU price (issue #497). ijurica asked for sample records across pricing models, and robmartin33 worried that excluding properties already held in other columns would hurt compatibility, so a MAY clause was added. TF-2 voted for PascalCase keys, though flanakin noted JSON usually uses camel case, and in August 2024 directed merging the two into one SkuPriceDetails column; flanakin and thecloudman preferred the name SKU Details. flanakin asked for SHOULD rather than MUST on consistent properties, fearing it would block support, but maintainers kept MUST because "no data is better than bad data". #530 covered charges without a SkuPriceId. Members approved it on 5 September 2024 and it merged.
summaries.516: AWS-ZachErdman's pull request, tied to #495, added a dedicated column describing what a SKU meters, first drafted as UsageType. Through TF-2, maintainers and members calls from August 2024, the group used naming spreadsheets and polls, settling on SKU Meter, with a revote that included alternatives from flanakin, who did not want the name to look chosen by Microsoft. ijurica wanted the column focused on the SKU and its nullability aligned with SkuId; AWS-ZachErdman said not every AWS SKU has a meter name, so values should not be forced. cnharris10 and ahullah noted that mixing coded and readable strings was a problem for a longer-term solution, not a blocker. udam-f2 asked for supporting content, which was added. Members approved it on September 19, 2024, and it merged that month.
summaries.519: For #404, shawnalpay proposed a ServiceSubcategory column giving finer groupings beneath each ServiceCategory. udam-f2 asked for short, non-marketing descriptions and questioned names such as Language AI, later renamed NLP; shawnalpay rewrote Networking as a model and applied that style elsewhere. Whether the column should be mandatory or optional was debated without a clear result in the thread. Answering a quoted suggestion to keep the categories in a separate repository, flanakin argued they must stay in the spec so versioned data stays consistent, and warned against frequent changes. After sessions with flanakin, shawnalpay added subcategories such as AI Platform and Endpoint Management and renamed several networking and storage ones, while the placement of search services was still being debated. Members approved it in September 2024 and it was merged.
summaries.523: Pull request #523, by gparker-at-sf, came out of #397 and proposed Capacity Reservation ID and Capacity Reservation Status columns. The main dispute was how firmly to require the ID: cnharris10 suggested SHOULD because AWS would not initially provide values, flanakin preferred MUST, and AWS-ZachErdman opposed MUST as unproven and wanted conformance possible without labelling used reservation charges. ijurica proposed requiring a status only when an ID is present, which AWS-ZachErdman endorsed. cnharris10's global uniqueness suggestion met the objection that other ID columns don't enforce it. A generic glossary entry for capacity reservation was added, and udam-f2 asked for supporting content explaining the SHOULD. Members approved it on 5 September 2024 and it merged.
summaries.524: cnharris10 renamed "commitment-based discount" and similar phrases to "commitment discount" throughout the spec to match the FinOps terminology page. The change was editorial. shawnalpay approved and suggested also scrubbing terms such as usage-based, spend-based and tier-based. Members approved it on 22 August 2024 and it merged.
summaries.530: kk09v's PR, dependent on #503, let providers without a SkuPriceId repeat SkuId as SkuPriceId when they include SkuPriceDetails, and reformatted the requirements as bullets. Task Force 2 asked for refinements and an offline discussion of edge cases. flanakin approved but asked that reformatting and content edits not be mixed in one PR. Members approved it on September 5, 2024, and it was merged.
summaries.533: For #532, ijurica proposed classing commitment discount purchase rows as Standard rather than Committed in PricingCategory, by adding an exception for purchases of the commitment itself. flanakin suggested dropping the link to CommitmentDiscountId so other purchase commitments fit, and cnharris10 suggested limiting Committed to usage charges; ijurica questioned whether commitments could never apply to purchases. Members approved it in September 2024, with ijurica to update the phrasing to match.
summaries.535: cnharris10 opened this PR to add an appendix of examples showing how commitment discount purchases and usage are modelled with and without flexibility. flanakin warned that calling it "size flexibility" would constrain later naming, so cnharris10 renamed it. At an October 2024 call, members agreed to keep it for v1.2 under a backfilled work item. rileyjenk and UdamDewaraja requested changes, asking that it move to the examples section and that the JSON samples become externally stored CSV files; cnharris10 split it into separate example files but preferred to leave format conversion to a later consistency review. ijurica asked for appendix links to sit outside normative requirements and for consistent column names and unit price terms. Members approved it on 27 March 2025, and it was merged that month.
summaries.539: cnharris10's PR was purely mechanical: it made the working_draft branch build by adding the capacity reservation columns to columns.mdpp and fixing linter issues, such as bullet style and spacing, in the capacity reservation and SKU column files. There was no content change or discussion, and it was merged in September 2024.
summaries.540: cnharris10 opened this in September 2024 after AWS-ZachErdman found the rule against altering user-defined tag keys caused collisions when a provider has several user-defined tag systems, such as AWS resource tags and cost categories or GCP tags and labels. It proposed prefixing all but one scheme. thecloudman and daviddinhgcp said GCP did not face the problem; cnharris10 replied that pushing tags into provider-specific columns defeated a single Tags column, and rileyjenk, udam-f2 and ijurica backed namespacing. thecloudman suggested organisational tagging standards. A January 2025 poll favoured Option 3, a prefixing approach. daviddinhgcp asked to delay and proposed keeping tags and labels separate; shawnalpay, cnharris10 and rileyjenk replied that Tags had existed since 1.0 Preview, citing #691. shawnalpay marked it complete in March 2025, noting Google Cloud's #788 for 1.3 scoping.
summaries.549: Pull request #549, by ijurica, set out to standardize how columns handle correction charges, allowing nulls for corrections except in cost metrics and defining value ranges. Because of deadlines, scope was cut to ConsumedUnit and ConsumedQuantity, with other columns left as they were for 1.1. cnharris10 proposed simpler requirements and putting 'usage' in the descriptions, and ijurica reworked them. Members approved it on 3 October 2024 and it merged.
summaries.550: Pull request #550, by cnharris10, edited CommitmentDiscountQuantity and CommitmentDiscountUnit during the 1.1 consistency review to add correction handling and cut duplicated clauses. ijurica set out what the columns should require for regular and correction charges and favoured a restructured Option B, while cnharris10 preferred Option A's minimal edits, arguing that months of approved work should not be reworked. ijurica then offered an Option C keeping the original flow as bullets. At TF-1 on 1 October 2024 the group agreed to defer readability improvements to a later 1.x release. ijurica also spotted that CommitmentDiscountUnit lacked the correction allowance given to the quantity column; the group backed ijurica's changes, cnharris10 integrated them, and Members approved the PR on 3 October 2024.
summaries.552: udam-f2 proposed ServiceSubcategory wording fixes agreed at a September 2024 consistency review meeting. ijurica suggested stating that each subcategory has exactly one parent ServiceCategory, asked whether FOCUS should define that parent, and suggested referencing the ServiceName column; arrarama asked how services that depend on other services would fit. shawnalpay approved, and members approved it on October 3, 2024, when it was merged.
summaries.557: ijurica proposed reviewing the normative requirements of every column and attribute, after two data producers had read FOCUS 1.0 differently, and drafting a template for writing them. TF-2 noted possible breaking changes and made it a backward-compatibility work item. ijurica built a requirements cookbook and a preview PR, #664, and asked members to review flagged columns in January 2025. No comment records the outcome; GitHub shows it closed as completed.
summaries.559: ahullah added notes on aggregation to cost, price and quantity columns to support commitment utilization calculations. ijurica said ConsumedQuantity had no double-counting issue, so that section was removed, and cnharris10 reworded the unit price notes to say values should not be summed. Members made the constraints advisory rather than mandatory and approved it on October 3, 2024. It merged in October 2024.
summaries.579: cnharris10's editorial PR marked commitment discount purchases with the PricingCategory value Standard. ijurica asked whether unused commitment rows should then be Standard or Committed, and cnharris10 said Committed, since they amortize a non-refundable prepurchase. TF-2 asked cnharris10 to open a separate PR clarifying the definitions. Members approved it on 3 October 2024 and it merged.
summaries.588: This editorial pull request by jpradocueva aligned column names and IDs in FOCUS 1.1 with the earlier editorial guidelines: display names in descriptions, column IDs in normative text and italic glossary terms. ijurica fixed links and noted that maintainers had decided to use attribute IDs in normative paragraphs while keeping attribute names in content constraints tables. Members approved it on October 8, 2024, and it was merged.
summaries.589: Mostly editorial: ijurica aligned how columns, attributes and glossary terms were referenced in several columns, following the version 1.1 editorial guidelines, and fixed missing or broken links. ijurica first favoured attribute names in normative text; after udam-f2 questioned this, the maintainers agreed to use attribute IDs in normative paragraphs. Members approved it in October 2024 and it was merged.
summaries.606: Issue #606, opened by jpradocueva in October 2024, tracked editorial pull requests applying the new editorial guidelines to columns after 1.1, mainly turning verbose normative statements into bullets. Members agreed in October 2024 to keep reviewing them as a group within two weeks, and later calls asked for reviews of batches such as #623 to #631 and #651 to #658. No comment records the outcome; GitHub shows it closed as completed.
summaries.615: kk09v proposed an Invoice ID column so practitioners could tie charges to provider invoices for reconciliation, chargeback and credit memos. shawnalpay asked for use cases and data examples. Lacking volunteers, maintainers asked ahullah to draft it; thecloudman compared provider invoicing and weighed a dedicated column against a metadata field, and narciso-cerezo explained that invoices are immutable. thecloudman added the column to #686, and shawnalpay closed the issue in May 2025.
summaries.616: shawnalpay opened this in October 2024 because FOCUS had been built around cloud providers and offered SaaS vendors no onramp; it proposed a time-boxed analysis of SaaS billing concepts leading to an initial MVP. mike-finopsorg reported strong demand from an APJ user group. Over the following months, task forces defined SaaS, built a billing model and provider matrix, and agreed to document commitment models such as burn-down, build-up and perpetual, plus commitment intervals; members gathered examples from providers including Datadog, Twilio, GitHub and Salesforce. In February 2025 GrinsteadJ argued that setting BilledCost to zero for marketplace-billed SaaS charges would block chargeback, proposing either filtering by invoice issuer or a new column. shawnalpay closed it in May 2025, moving unfinished SaaS scenario examples to #989.
summaries.619: ijurica opened this work item in October 2024 to give practitioners standardized SKU and SKU price properties such as term, tier and region, superseding several earlier issues. Calls split the scope to protect v1.2, assigned it to TF2, and organized a practitioner survey, with flanakin drafting it and jpradocueva building the form. shawnalpay closed it in May 2025 once all action items were complete.
summaries.642: This administrative pull request by jpradocueva prepared Candidate Release 1.1 for final approval as FOCUS 1.1. Members approved it on their November 7, 2024 call, and the Steering Committee ratified it the same day. mike-finopsorg recorded the approval, and it was merged in November 2024.
summaries.643: AWS-ZachErdman opened this work item in November 2024 to define what a breaking change is in FOCUS, how to weigh its cost to practitioners against its benefit, and how to build that into the spec process. Meeting notes through January 2025 assigned drafting to AWS-ZachErdman and rileyjenk, and asked beau-nelford-anglepoint to classify use cases by whether they changed between 1.0 and 1.1. No comment records the outcome; GitHub shows it closed as completed.
summaries.651: This editorial pull request by jpradocueva, under #606, converted ChargeCategory's normative statements into bullet points. flanakin suggested putting each requirement on its own line and dropping the words "This column". The group approved it on the December 5, 2024 Members' call, with further changes to follow under #557, and it was merged in December 2024.
summaries.652: This editorial pull request by jpradocueva, under #606, turned ContractedCost's normative statements into bullet points. flanakin suggested splitting compound requirements and making the wording consistent. The group agreed to work in stages, converting to bullets first and refining them later under #557, and approved it on the December 5, 2024 Members' call. It was merged in December 2024.
summaries.654: This editorial PR by jpradocueva reformatted the ListCost normative statement as bullet points. kk09v supported it but noted that ListCost was mandatory while ListUnitPrice was conditional, with no guidance for calculating cost without a list price; ijurica said the glossary link was intentional and proposed handling the gaps in #557. The group agreed to work in stages, and the PR was merged in December 2024.
summaries.676: ijurica's PR for #314 clarified the SkuId, SkuPriceId and SkuPriceDetails columns. ijurica asked whether the presence conditions could be merged and when SkuId may equal SkuPriceId, and recorded TF-2 assumptions that SkuPriceId should exclude variable pricing properties and have one parent SkuId. cnharris10 requested changes, asking whether the edits let providers do as they pleased (flanakin said the intent was unchanged) and objecting to the single-parent rule with an RDS size-flexibility example. UdamDewaraja and ljadvey opposed requiring one SkuId across single and multi-AZ offerings; mike-finopsorg and rileyjenk agreed those lines went too far, and flanakin deferred several to a future release. UdamDewaraja questioned typing SkuPriceDetails as a String, and kk09v moved its requirements into #683. Members approved it on April 3, 2025, and it merged in April 2025.
summaries.683: Pull request #683, by kk09v, defined preferred keys for the SKU Price Details column (#619), narrowed to that column at shawnalpay's request. kk09v added an F_ prefix for FOCUS-defined keys and tightened them to MUST, but flanakin strongly objected that it made FOCUS feel second-class and withheld approval; shawnalpay agreed and suggested a reserved list instead. After a working group vote, provider-defined keys took an x_ prefix instead. aws-letianfeng requested changes over what InputOutput covered and how burstable 'up to' values work, leading to separate network and disk properties and a baseline-value rule. Other threads debated naming such as CoreCount and Iops, null versus empty objects, and reverting the data type to JSON. Members approved it on 3 April 2025 and it merged.
summaries.686: thecloudman opened this pull request for #615 to define an InvoiceId column and supporting content. After talking with rileyjenk, thecloudman added notes proposing a separate invoice ID table mapping invoices to rows, so providers would not need to update every row when an invoice is issued. cnharris10 asked whether the wording made the column conditional; mike-finopsorg read it as present, and null when no invoice applies. udam-f2 worried that providers such as GCP cannot restate exported data and found the uniqueness wording too strong. ijurica proposed many normative rewrites, and ljadvey and UdamDewaraja debated saying issued invoices. thecloudman dropped a rule tying each invoice to one billing account and added an editor's note on unresolved credit handling. Members approved it on February 27, 2025, and it was merged.
summaries.691: beau-nelford-anglepoint's PR implemented #540, putting all user-defined tags in the Tags column and setting rules for providers with multiple tag schemes, following an earlier community survey. cnharris10 answered aws-letianfeng's question about tag keys containing "/" by saying providers must reserve any prefix they define, as AWS does with "aws:". ijurica suggested handling provider tag prefixes in metadata as part of #540. flanakin asked whether labels and categories clearly count as tags, wanted a MUST NOT with an exception split in two, and proposed requiring prefixes to be published in metadata; cnharris10 defended the valueless-tag exception and kept publication open-ended. kk09v confirmed exactly one user-defined scheme stays unprefixed. UdamDewaraja and shawnalpay fixed casing and punctuation. Members approved it on February 27, 2025, and it was merged.
summaries.711: shawnalpay opened this action item in February 2025 to track continued collaboration on #676. flanakin and kk09v committed to a draft by March 12 for Task Force 2 review ahead of the March 13 PR freeze. It was closed in March 2025 once #676 came out of draft. The thread is mostly housekeeping.
summaries.716: A routine action item: shawnalpay opened it to gather reviews and approvals of #691, including whether an appendix was needed. shawnalpay chased aws-letianfeng, through jasonwucp, and flanakin, who completed a review. The issue was closed after #691 was approved at the Members meeting in February 2025.
summaries.780: rileyjenk proposed BilledCost changes (#616) to prevent double counting between vendor and marketplace FOCUS records, tying BilledCost sums to invoices from the invoice issuer. Reviewers debated the wording: cnharris10 suggested it SHOULD match and MUST NOT exceed payable invoices, while flanakin urged being ambitious and letting data generators document coverage gaps. thecloudman proposed saying "finalized" invoices rather than listing estimate invoices, and ijurica asked whether such charges should be zero and whether naming the invoice issuer added anything. UdamDewaraja found combining billing period, billing account and InvoiceId problematic. After TF-2 on March 27, ijurica suggested matching the sum for a given InvoiceId to that invoice's payable amount. shawnalpay asked rileyjenk to resolve open threads before the members vote. Members approved it on April 3, 2025, and it merged that month.
summaries.787: For #557 and FOCUS 1.2, ijurica set out guidelines for writing column normative requirements and rewrote a first set of columns to match, with the rest in #798; reviewers were asked to flag unintended changes. flanakin questioned dropping "globally" from globally unique identifiers, doubted providers could guarantee unique billing account names, a point thecloudman echoed, and found "exclusive ending bound" unclear. shawnalpay resisted changing requirement strength within a consistency review, keeping ChargeDescription length a SHOULD. qquigley asked why both SHOULD and RECOMMENDED appeared; ijurica said RECOMMENDED marked presence rules tied to feature levels. smokemonster99 queried renamed column references, which ijurica said followed the editorial guidelines. Unresolved points went to a list of discussion topics. Members approved it in March 2025 and it was merged.
summaries.798: This was the second part of ijurica's rewrite of column normative requirements under the #557 guidelines, with #787 covering the other columns. ijurica flagged deliberate changes already agreed in TF-1: fixing CommitmentDiscountQuantity's positive-only value range as a bug, rewording EffectiveCost rules for unused commitments, and aligning nullability for quantity and unit pairs. flanakin proposed EffectiveCost wording linking purchase and usage costs, and answered thecloudman's doubt about tax examples. SkuPriceDetails was declared a String with key-value format, and another SkuPriceDetails change was reverted after UdamDewaraja raised a concern, with follow-up logged as #855. cnharris10 and ijurica reworked how the Tags requirements were grouped, and smokemonster99 caught typos. Members approved it in April 2025 and it was merged.
summaries.807: shawnalpay opened this action item to resolve the editor's note in the Invoice ID column. The fix in #828 waited on whether #675 would make version 1.2; when shawnalpay judged that unlikely, thecloudman was told to proceed without it. The group suggested removing the editor's note and adding a note to the supporting document, and shawnalpay closed the item in March 2025 after confirming with thecloudman.
summaries.810: shawnalpay opened this action item in February 2025 to prevent double counting in Effective Cost, alongside the Billed Cost work. rileyjenk narrowed it so the Effective Cost question would not hold up the Billed Cost changes. shawnalpay suggested it was complete once #780 left draft, but after speaking with rileyjenk recorded in March 2025 that the work was postponed to 1.3.
summaries.828: thecloudman proposed credit-handling requirements for the InvoiceId column (#615). shawnalpay suggested condensing them and asked ahullah and ijurica to review, mike-finopsorg proposed rules for credits in the current billing period, and flanakin made editorial points. After TF-2 discussion, thecloudman moved the credit handling into supporting content and set the feature level to Recommended at ijurica's suggestion. Members approved it in March 2025 and it merged.
summaries.844: rileyjenk added to the spec a clarification on how FOCUS uses Semantic Versioning, agreed at an August 2024 maintainers meeting but never written in (#643). shawnalpay suggested README wording. Members approved it on March 27, 2025, and it was merged that month.
summaries.848: shawnalpay proposed four columns for prices set in a virtual or different currency (PricingCurrency, PricingCurrencyEffectiveCost, PricingCurrencyListUnitPrice and PricingCurrencyContractedUnitPrice), replacing #799 because some members rejected redefining existing unit price columns; existing columns stayed unchanged. cnharris10 supported the aim but feared moving too fast without modelled data, so mike-finopsorg shared a sample sheet. thecloudman asked whether a priced cost column duplicated Billed Cost, and ijurica proposed simpler presence conditions. daviddinhgcp proposed separate token and local currency columns; mike-finopsorg replied that conversion works the same for national and virtual currencies and extra columns would widen the spec. On March 31, 2025 maintainers struck the exchange rate column and deferred exchange rates to a future release. Members approved the PR on April 3, 2025, and it was merged that day.
summaries.854: shawnalpay opened this March 2025 issue as a running list of 1.2 consistency review tasks, such as file naming, CSV examples, a stray table row and the changelog, each spun off into its own action item, and ijurica proposed more. At the April 7, 2025 maintainers meeting, revisiting "amortization" in EffectiveCost and settling row versus charge versus record were deferred to a future release. The thread doesn't record its closure.
summaries.873: This mostly editorial PR by flanakin removed unnecessary references to "row" from column definitions. jpradocueva asked whether "charge" should be italicised or linked, which became moot when the word was dropped, and shawnalpay opposed ijurica's suggestion to describe account types as names rather than identifiers. Members approved it on 17 April 2025, and it was merged.
summaries.892: Matt-Cowsert's first PR, under #877, fixed typos and simple grammar issues across the spec for the 1.2 release. shawnalpay asked to back out an edit to a metadata example because #900 would rework that file, and Matt-Cowsert agreed; ijurica moved a separate fix, a missing "not", to another item. shawnalpay approved, Members approved it on April 17, 2025, and it was merged.
summaries.905: ijurica proposed fixing post-merge inconsistencies in the SKU and SKU Price columns for AI #902, plus best-effort editorial changes. shawnalpay requested changes, agreeing to remove a duplicated SkuPriceDetails requirement but saying the consistency review was not the time to reword normative requirements or rewrite the description. Members approved the PR on April 17, 2025, and it was merged that day.
summaries.910: ijurica proposed clarifying that FOCUS-defined SkuPriceDetails properties take precedence over equivalent provider-defined ones. shawnalpay questioned treating this as a fix during consistency review, and kk09v read the rule as intentionally requiring both; it was postponed to 1.3 in April 2025. In July ijurica adopted kk09v's rewording and reverted a SHOULD-to-MUST change after kk09v objected. Members approved it on September 4, 2025.
summaries.914: ijurica's pull request (#913) made best-effort editorial adjustments, mainly to column specs, adding links to glossary terms and columns and aligning formatting with the editorial guidelines. shawnalpay approved it with one small suggestion on Charge Category. Members approved it on April 17, 2025, and it merged.
summaries.956: Matt-Cowsert opened this in May 2025 asking FOCUS to carry provider-calculated cost splits below the machine level, such as containers, pods and tasks, citing AWS, GCP, OCI and Azure features; many organisations registered support. shawnalpay argued the data adds rows and columns, so practitioners must be able to opt in (#1091, #1093). UdamDewaraja objected to calling it shared cost allocation, and TF-2 renamed it in July 2025. TF-2 compared split lines, double-entry rows and a secondary dataset; a poll (#1322) favoured split lines, while rileyjenk and jasonwucp worried about breaking existing reports. The group agreed allocations must reconcile to the original charge, be flagged and use a JSON details column (#1383). #1394, stewarded by kk09v and qquigley, was approved and merged in September 2025, closing the request as complete.
summaries.958: Matt-Cowsert asked for an indicator showing which non-negotiated discount programs, such as commitment discounts or SaaS public pricing tiers, a charge was eligible for, to support coverage and savings-rate analysis. qquigley supported a simple boolean but warned that hypothetical cost columns could taint reporting; shawnalpay suggested a JSON column of eligibility flags. Scoped for 1.3, it was repeatedly bumped and then descoped in August 2025. From November 2025 SanjnaSrivatsaVMware sponsored and drafted it in Task Force 3, where the group chose JSON over a boolean, broadened scope beyond commitment discounts after cnharris10 raised hybrid SaaS cases, added capacity reservations, and made negotiated programs a MAY. The name became Commitment Program Eligibility Details, and shawnalpay closed the issue in April 2026 after #1882 and #2025 merged.
summaries.962: Matt-Cowsert asked in May 2025 for an overarching correction-handling attribute, because correction rules were scattered across individual columns and practitioners needed to reconcile corrections with invoices. Most comments were task force updates from shawnalpay. ijurica split the work into several PRs, including #1241, #1242 and #1245 tightening existing column requirements, #1368 for the attribute and #1434 for examples. In October 2025 the maintainers deferred #1368, refactored as #1501, until an Invoice dataset (#1500) could ground rules on when data generators may revise invoiced data. By January 2026 #1501 covered both delivery handling and correction handling, and in March ijurica and rileyjenk agreed to split it further. Members merged #1434 and #1501, and shawnalpay closed the request as complete in April 2026.
summaries.976: Matt-Cowsert asked FOCUS to represent contract-negotiated commitments, such as burn-down and build-up agreements, so practitioners could track progress against them; NASA, Autodesk, Atlassian, Google and others added support. Task Force 1 began in June 2025 with goals of giving each negotiated commitment an ID, linking usage to it and describing its terms. ijurica noted a single contract ID could not show drawdown against individual line items, and shawnalpay floated a mandatory Contract ID with an optional Commitment ID. shawnalpay renamed the request and opened #1327, then #1350. In August 2025 most participants favored always requiring the proposed JSON datapoints for usability, while cnharris10 and partly richkreitz prioritized dataset size. #1350 merged in September 2025, closing the request, with follow-on work in #1459.
summaries.982: Matt-Cowsert opened this in May 2025 because ambiguous EffectiveCost and BilledCost definitions led data generators to implement them inconsistently, including a rule zeroing BilledCost for all marketplace purchases. Through 2025 Task Force 3 split over partial-upfront commitments: rileyjenk wanted billed cost distributed to usage records, while ijurica wanted it kept on purchase records. In September 2025 the work was cut from 1.3. For 1.4 the group reframed the problem as accuracy rather than double counting, adopted three milestones and, as shawnalpay urged, avoided the term amortization. Definitions were refined in #1678, and #1966 rewrote the normative requirements around covered and covering charges and the invoice issuer. After #1966 and #2022 were approved and merged, shawnalpay closed it as complete in April 2026.
summaries.1024: Matt-Cowsert asked for clearer SkuPriceDetails rules, because the wording implied both a FOCUS-defined property and its provider-defined equivalent must appear, rather than preferring the FOCUS-defined one. flanakin supported it but said a PR would be better than task force time, and ijurica noted FOCUS-defined properties were new in 1.2. shawnalpay closed it as complete in September 2025 after #910 merged.
summaries.1026: Matt-Cowsert proposed replacing RECOMMENDED with SHOULD throughout the spec, since RFC 2119 treats the two as equivalent and mixing them could confuse implementers. Matt-Cowsert asked whether practitioners had reported problems; jpradocueva knew of none, and qquigley supported it while expecting it to be a low priority. In February 2026 shawnalpay said #1647 had already done the work and closed the request.
summaries.1055: Matt-Cowsert asked to clarify the ambiguous Provider, Publisher and Invoice Issuer columns, deferred from 1.2. jasonwucp urged setting breaking-change criteria first, and ijurica flagged inconsistent display names. Task Force 3 agreed in September 2025 to deprecate Provider and Publisher in favor of service provider and host provider columns, and shortened the deprecation window to one release. shawnalpay closed it in October 2025 after #1139, #1505 and #1524 were approved.
summaries.1057: Matt-Cowsert requested a separate dataset of a provider's SKUs and prices for lookups, joins and pre-purchase estimation. shawnalpay asked for scope and use cases and distinguished a SKU dataset from a SKU Price dataset. From May 2026 shawnalpay drafted a model and #2424, which Matt-Cowsert stewarded during shawnalpay's leave. Task Force 1 worked through tier boundaries, PricingCategory, dropping ChargeFrequency, snapshot versus history, and the dataset's condition, keeping IncludesUnitPricing in September 2026. The longest dispute was two price columns on one row versus one row per price under a single UnitPrice; shawnalpay argued for rows to avoid fabricated effective dates, while flanakin's queryability concern stayed open. Members approved releasing the dataset as a preview on October 22, 2026, and GitHub shows the issue closed as completed on 31 October 2026.
summaries.1059: ijurica opened this in May 2025 because FOCUS had no formal guidelines for writing attribute specifications, risking inconsistent or unclear requirements; the plan was to write guidelines and apply them to existing attributes without material changes. shawnalpay pointed to precedent PRs #787 and #798 and later urged priority, since compound requirements such as those in Discount Handling were hard to turn into conformance rules. The item moved between task forces and went undiscussed for months until February 2026, when ijurica presented #1967 (guidelines) and #1981 (refactoring), rephrasing requirements as verifiable states for the FOCUS Validator. A few deliberate material changes were accepted and others deferred. For binding requirements to custom columns, mike-finopsorg proposed a hybrid approach. shawnalpay closed it as complete in April 2026 after #1967, #1981 and #2166 merged.
summaries.1070: Issue #1070, opened by Matt-Cowsert in May 2025, argued that FOCUS's use of 'commitment discount' excluded negotiated commitments and assumed a burn-down model, which caused problems for SaaS. shawnalpay asked how it overlapped with #976, and ijurica gathered the existing glossary definitions. In September 2025 it was renamed and moved from 1.3 to 1.4 as tied to Contract Commitment work in #1459. It closed in March 2026, completed via #1964.
summaries.1073: Matt-Cowsert requested a way to show the cloud provider hosting a SaaS service such as Snowflake, which the Provider, Publisher and Invoice Issuer definitions did not capture. shawnalpay reframed it as a Host Provider request, questioned its use cases and made it depend on #1055. Matt-Cowsert later noted its scope was covered by #1139, and shawnalpay closed it as complete in October 2025 after the related PRs merged.
summaries.1082: Matt-Cowsert asked that the spec state every charge on an invoice must appear in FOCUS data, so BilledCost reconciles to the invoice. shawnalpay pressed for taxes and indirect charges such as training to be covered. TF-3 drafted an invoice handling attribute in #1321, debating SHOULD versus MUST, duplication and payable splits, and kept a single MUST. #1321 merged and the request closed as complete in September 2025.
summaries.1090: robmartin33 asked in May 2025 for FOCUS to be organised as related datasets, for easier use in BI tools, so finer detail could be added without bloating the main dataset. shawnalpay strongly supported it as a star schema, referencing #1006. In June 2025 the group agreed a six-week spike, ruling out a star schema for 1.3. Task Force 2 then produced design principles (#1150) and dataset definitions (#1337), rejecting fact and dimension terminology as too database-specific in favour of names like FOCUS Cost and Usage plus machine-readable IDs, and requiring datasets to be independent but joinable. Maintainers adopted dataset-level normative requirements, and #1431 tied attributes to datasets. A second dataset was left to #976 and editorial cleanup to consistency review. shawnalpay closed it as complete in October 2025.
summaries.1091: Matt-Cowsert asked in May 2025 for data generators to let practitioners choose which columns to export, and maintainers debated whether this was within FOCUS's remit. #1816 first added aggregation and time granularity; shawnalpay objected that aggregation belonged to consumers, and flanakin disagreed but accepted dropping it, which thecloudman and mike-finopsorg supported. #1816 was approved and merged, and the issue was closed in February 2026.
summaries.1094: Matt-Cowsert asked that FOCUS datasets carry custom x_ columns for any native billing data not covered by FOCUS columns, so practitioners could rely on FOCUS alone. ijurica added correlation use cases, such as carrying a provider's unique charge ID as a custom column. flanakin said only MUST would achieve the goal, though SHOULD might win provider buy-in, and in January 2026 opened #1800 with a new Scenario Completeness attribute. A provider-side request to soften MUST to SHOULD was settled by keeping MUST while letting data generators default to a subset of columns. The group made correlation a separate SHOULD and, in March 2026, simplified the core rule to include all native columns except documented, justified exclusions. #1800 merged and shawnalpay closed the issue in March 2026.
summaries.1124: Matt-Cowsert opened this request because practitioners could not tell which charges can be tagged or where a tag value came from. With kk09v and qquigley as sponsors and work starting in 1.4, TF-2 widened it from resource to charge tagging after cnharris10 noted SaaS tags without resources, and ruled out SKUs as the basis. From eleven candidate structures the group chose a key-driven TagDetails column alongside Tags, after kk09v's BigQuery tests, drafted as #1904. An AWS test showed data growing seven to eight times, tying it to column selection (#1091). In March 2026 shawnalpay opposed adding Recommended columns; maintainers found little support for #1904 as written, felt the scope had grown without re-review, and believed time had run out in the release.
