summaries.1139: rileyjenk opened this pull request in June 2025 for #1055 and #1073, after feedback that the Provider and Publisher columns were confusing. It deprecated PublisherName and ProviderName and added Service Provider and Host Provider columns, the latter for vendors running on other providers' infrastructure. Because this was FOCUS's first deprecation, shawnalpay asked for a summary and a link to the deprecation guidelines. flanakin objected that renaming Provider would force customers to change their queries and suggested calling the new column Host; rileyjenk replied that Host alone was ambiguous and naming was better fixed now. Reviewers also debated whether a FinOps vendor is a data generator, with editorial follow-ups moved to #1226 and #1336. Members approved it on October 16, 2025, and it was merged that month.
summaries.1240: Matt-Cowsert opened this action item in August 2025 to draft an invoice-handling attribute, describing how invoiced charges relate to the FOCUS dataset, and review it with members (#1321). TF-3 asked for more specificity, chose to reference charge category requirements rather than repeat them, and parked the charge versus row debate (#1027). In August 2025 shawnalpay asked to close it once the draft was ready for member review, and Matt-Cowsert agreed.
summaries.1321: Matt-Cowsert proposed an invoice handling attribute for FR #1082, requiring FOCUS datasets to cover every invoiced charge. shawnalpay asked for it to be applied to every affected column and for Invoice ID to cover all charges; flanakin objected that one billing period can have several invoices, so the original wording returned with a clarification. UdamDewaraja wanted prepaid usage statements included, warned invoices cannot be expected to use FOCUS terms, and argued the core rule was that totals per invoice ID match the invoice. flanakin asked where the line lay; ijurica floated limiting it to IT costs, and shawnalpay and ijurica proposed scoping it to invoices issued to a billing account. Task Force 3 struck duplicative requirements. Members approved it on September 25, 2025; it merged the next day.
summaries.1334: shawnalpay's action item was to draft a PR adding contract attributes such as start date and amount, needed to complete #976 beyond the columns in #1327. It was briefly blocked on #1090 until the August 11, 2025 Maintainers call set a direction. shawnalpay drafted #1350, revised it after TF1 feedback on contractual commitments, and closed the item in September 2025 once #1350 left draft.
summaries.1336: shawnalpay opened this action item in August 2025 to review the spec's 149 uses of "provider" and replace them with terms such as service provider, host provider or data generator, following #1055 and #1139. shawnalpay urged starting early in 1.3 development; rileyjenk volunteered but preferred waiting until spec development finished. The work landed in #1567, which was approved and merged, and the item closed in November 2025.
summaries.1337: Pull request #1337, by mike-finopsorg, reorganized the repository layout to support multiple FOCUS datasets (#1090). shawnalpay requested that the existing dataset be called Cost and Usage rather than the FOCUS dataset, since any FOCUS dataset should count as one. flanakin objected that duplicating columns per dataset would not scale; shawnalpay replied that maintainers had reached consensus on it in August. Members approved it on 28 August 2025 and it merged.
summaries.1350: For #976, shawnalpay proposed a ContractApplied JSON column linking each cost row to the contract commitments it counts toward, plus a new Contract Commitment dataset describing those commitments. kk09v argued for a true JSON object format with a defined schema, which led to #1383 and kk09v's #1462, and ijurica wanted custom properties declared in metadata. After flanakin asked how several contracts could apply to one charge, ContractId moved inside the array. cnharris10 questioned having both type and description columns, and marc-perreaut's idea for handling values redundant with other columns was weighed against added complexity. Maintainers let data generators omit inapplicable cost, quantity or unit values, and BillingCurrency replaced a separate currency column. shawnalpay offered to defer ContractCommitmentType to #1459. Members approved it in September 2025 and it was merged.
summaries.1380: shawnalpay opened this issue in August 2025 to collect work for the 1.3 consistency review, planned for October 16 to 30. Contributors logged many items, each turned into an action item or pull request: adding Requirements subheaders (#1508), restructuring supporting content (#1510), replacing "term" with "duration" (#1493), JSON string versus object typing (#1480), standardizing .mdpp files (#1512), drafting changelog entries, fixing the Commitment definition to include spend (#1514), clarifying "data artifact" and "FOCUS dataset" usage (#1515), and ijurica's EffectiveCost wording and nesting suggestions. Matt-Cowsert reported TF-3 agreed to revert display-name changes on deprecated columns; shawnalpay argued that belonged in #1139 rather than consistency review. Remaining items were assigned in October task force meetings, and the issue closed when 1.3 was released in December 2025.
summaries.1382: shawnalpay reported that the HTML and PDF builder numbered duplicate anchors for columns used in several datasets, which would break links as datasets were added, and proposed prefixing anchors with the dataset name. mike-finopsorg suggested extending the vendored Markdown-PP tool to build anchors from the full heading path, and shawnalpay widened the scope to name overlaps between attributes and supported features. It was completed through #1656 in January 2026.
summaries.1389: mike-finopsorg proposed moving normative requirements that apply to a whole dataset, chiefly column presence rules, into each dataset definition, rephrased so the dataset carries the requirement. shawnalpay saw it as a subset of #1090, and the work was combined with #1796. Task Force 2 confirmed the approach in January 2026. It closed via #1865 in February 2026, was reopened for #2138, and closed again in April 2026.
summaries.1394: kk09v and qquigley proposed provider-calculated split cost allocation (#956), adding AllocatedResourceId, AllocatedResourceName, AllocatedMethodId, AllocatedTags and a details column, plus an attribute, a supported feature and glossary terms. TF-2 reshaped the details column into an array of objects with a JSON schema, later named AllocatedMethodDetails, and moved the method into its own column. jpradocueva asked that requirements target dataset entities rather than providers, and rileyjenk objected to requiring providers to support a feature, so kk09v softened the wording. flanakin questioned the term "allocated method" and whether ratios were fractions or percentages, and Cosmos DB cases went to #1479. shawnalpay pressed for a change summary, a fixed PDF build and resolved conflicts. Members approved it on 25 September 2025 and it merged.
summaries.1396: Matt-Cowsert opened this action item in August 2025 to resolve review comments on #1394, about provider-calculated split cost allocation, ahead of the 1.3 release. TF-2 worked through the comments over several weeks, and qquigley asked whether a name change to allocated method details had been agreed. In September 2025 shawnalpay declared it done after members reviewed #1394 with no open threads.
summaries.1431: shawnalpay proposed this for #1090 because the spec said attributes applied to all FOCUS datasets, which would be inaccurate once more existed; it associated every current attribute with the Cost and Usage dataset. flanakin questioned a line on when datasets are required, and shawnalpay explained only Cost and Usage is always required. ijurica suggested more dataset glossary terms. Members approved it on September 11, 2025, and it was merged.
summaries.1446: flanakin added "Name" to the display names of InvoiceIssuerName, ProviderName and PublisherName so they matched their column IDs (#1055). shawnalpay asked for a full scrub of other references and worried about overlap with #1139, which would deprecate Publisher; ijurica asked that descriptions begin with the column name. Members approved it on October 2, 2025, and it was merged that month.
summaries.1458: shawnalpay noted in September 2025 that spec text often assumed "a FOCUS dataset" meant the Cost and Usage dataset, citing Column Handling wording raised by ijurica, and asked for a scrub. After TF-2 discussion, Matt-Cowsert added it to the 1.3 consistency review (#1380). Matt-Cowsert closed it in October 2025 after the related pull request was approved at the members meeting.
summaries.1459: shawnalpay proposed in September 2025 extending the Contract Commitment dataset, founded in 1.3 by #1350 under #976, with columns for balances, scope rules, attestation and commitment models. It was paired with #1070 for 1.4, and Task Force 1 asked for use cases, examples and supported features. A data model drafted in January 2026 became PR #1924. shawnalpay closed it in March 2026 as completed via #1924, continuing in #1938.
summaries.1493: shawnalpay proposed using "period" consistently for lengths of time, replacing "term" and "duration", because #1350's contract commitments needed "term" to mean a contract provision. aws-jrmarks and robmartin33 asked to keep a Term glossary entry that points readers to Period, which shawnalpay added. ijurica suggested defining period as a time window, and SatyaVandrangi1 asked to avoid the word "condition". Members approved it and it merged in October 2025.
summaries.1500: rileyjenk requested an Invoice dataset so finance teams could reconcile FOCUS data against invoices. qquigley urged involving finance personas, and beau-nelford-anglepoint offered support. From November 2025 shawnalpay led modeling in Task Force 1 with finance experts, Matt-Cowsert gathered data generator input, and thecloudman asked for an FX rate column. #1900 advanced toward member review in February 2026, and shawnalpay closed the issue in April 2026 when #2100 merged.
summaries.1501: shawnalpay opened this pull request for #962 to add Correction Handling and Delivery Handling attributes and rework Invoice Handling. In October 2025 maintainers closed it, deferring the work until an Invoice dataset existed (#1500), but work resumed in 2026. The final version defined Replacement, Delta and Ledger correction styles and Overwrite and Append delivery, and moved Invoice Handling to an appendix. Matt-Cowsert recorded a decision not to rename the ChargeClass value "Correction", since that would be a breaking change. rileyjenk and pydi-aws warned that limits on correcting closed billing periods could deter vendors, while ijurica held that data must be accurate before being marked final; rileyjenk and ijurica converged on separating invoice status from data delivery status. Members approved it on April 2, 2026, and it was merged that month.
summaries.1513: Mostly editorial: shawnalpay bundled simple consistency fixes for the 1.3 consistency review under #1380. shawnalpay asked whether reordering requirements would change their conformance IDs, and the Maintainers confirmed in October 2025 that the IDs would stay durable. ijurica contributed edits to the dataset overview. Members approved it without objections in October 2025.
summaries.1518: ijurica's editorial PR reduced the nesting of several CommitmentDiscountQuantity requirements from three levels to two, with no material change, on the assumption that this suited conformance work better. Matt-Cowsert approved after a TF-2 review, saying it simplified the null check, and jpradocueva approved pending a check against #1209. Members approved it on 16 October 2025 and it merged.
summaries.1536: Mostly mechanical: davidearney updated the Requirements headers in column files from allocatedresourceid.md to chargeperiodend.md for #1508. shawnalpay requested changes because a trailing colon broke the PDF build and the introductory requirements sentence had to stay, following example PR #1509. davidearney fixed both, and Members approved it without objection on October 30, 2025, when it merged.
summaries.1550: shawnalpay noted in October 2025 that Section 1.8 wrongly said no conformance validators existed. mike-finopsorg offered three options: remove the section, link only the foundation's validator, or list other tools too. Matt-Cowsert preferred linking the validator without implying an exhaustive list. mike-finopsorg drafted text saying third-party tools may exist and none is mandated; it went into #1513, which members approved in October 2025.
summaries.1557: This editorial PR by davidearney standardised the Requirements headers for the columns from ChargePeriodStart through Tags. shawnalpay requested changes so that each column also kept a lead-in sentence saying it adheres to the requirements that follow, as agreed in #1536. Members approved it without objections on 30 October 2025, and it was merged that day.
summaries.1559: Editorial: for #1508, davidearney changed the Requirements headers of the contract commitment columns to match the rest of the spec. shawnalpay requested changes, asking that every column keep a lead-in sentence saying it adheres to the following requirements, following a pattern agreed in #1536. jpradocueva approved, and members approved it without objections in October 2025.
summaries.1566: ijurica applied the new dataset-level normative requirement guidelines to the Cost and Usage and Contract Commitment datasets. shawnalpay asked why DiscountHandling had moved and suggested alphabetical order, but accepted ijurica's explanation that the order put technical requirements before business ones, per the forthcoming #1529. Members approved it without objections on 30 October 2025, and it was merged.
summaries.1567: rileyjenk opened this PR to apply four entity terms consistently, service provider, host provider, data generator and invoice issuer, in place of loose uses of provider and publisher. rileyjenk renamed the new split cost allocation feature as service-provider-calculated, but the group voted for data generator, and shawnalpay committed those renames per an October 2025 TF-2 agreement. shawnalpay requested changes while agreeing with about 80% of the edits, and resolved heavy merge conflicts. ijurica supplied line-specific fixes and flagged broken titles and anchors left by the renaming. Approval was postponed to no later than 6 November 2025, when members approved it without objections, and it merged.
summaries.1570: Matt-Cowsert's PR, for #1458, added explicit "Cost and Usage" dataset references across column definitions and an appendix example. shawnalpay requested changes, agreeing with the appendix edits but objecting to naming the dataset in attributes, since the 1.3 team had agreed that link belongs in dataset requirements. Matt-Cowsert removed those references, shawnalpay approved, and Members approved it on October 30, 2025, when it was merged.
summaries.1582: shawnalpay opened this action item in November 2025 to fix anchor links for columns sharing a name across datasets and to document how anchors work, per #1569. ijurica noted that the PDF outline showed more heading levels than the on-page contents. mike-finopsorg opened #1656 for the link fix and asked for a separate feature request about the contents. No comment records the outcome; GitHub shows it closed as completed.
summaries.1645: qquigley's PR, under #1380, fixed a copy-and-paste error and clarified the split cost example. shawnalpay relayed mike-finopsorg's suggestion to state that the ContractApplied and AllocatedMethodDetails examples describe a single Cost and Usage row, so readers do not assume AllocatedRatio sums to 1. Members approved it on December 4, 2025, and jpradocueva noted the change also went to the candidate_recommendation branch, citing #1649.
summaries.1647: jpradocueva opened this pull request for #1646 to replace every RECOMMENDED normative statement with SHOULD. shawnalpay and ijurica asked for the editorial and normative requirements guidelines to be updated too, and maintainers set it to draft on December 1, 2025 until the guidelines stopped distinguishing SHOULD from RECOMMENDED. ijurica listed further places to change in the introduction and requirements model guidelines, and kk09v suggested rewordings in several column files. On December 15 maintainers also agreed to strike OPTIONAL from the allowed keywords. Matt-Cowsert confirmed that timwright2000 for Google and vikramdesai01 for Microsoft were content with the change. Members approved it without objection on December 18, 2025, and it was merged that month.
summaries.1656: Pull request #1656, by mike-finopsorg, was mechanical work fixing HTML and PDF anchor links for columns used in more than one dataset (#1582). ijurica asked for Metadata section links to be fixed too and listed broken ones, which mike-finopsorg corrected over several passes. Matt-Cowsert requested two link fixes in the provider name files, which shawnalpay committed. Members approved it on 8 January 2026 and it merged.
summaries.1661: An editorial PR in which narlaadbe fixed minor typos for #1541. shawnalpay and jpradocueva approved it, and Members approved it without objections on December 11, 2025, when it merged.
summaries.1676: shawnalpay asked for the applicability criteria that decide when conditional columns must be present to be defined in the spec itself, not only in the downstream Requirements Model. mike-finopsorg asked whether criteria should be defined first and cited in normative text, or derived from it. shawnalpay's #2351 was merged in May 2026; the issue was reopened to add conditions to column constraint tables via #2423, and closed in July 2026.
summaries.1678: ijurica opened this PR, the first milestone of #982, to rewrite the definitions of Billed Cost and Effective Cost and remove their outdated glossary entries. robmartin33 objected to framing them as cash-based and accrual-based accounting, Matt-Cowsert wanted a section on two practitioner challenges cut, and a TF-3 meeting on 9 January 2026 agreed the wording. ljadvey warned that dropping amortization from the definition would leave practitioners asking where net amortized costs are; shawnalpay suggested citing amortization as an example. udam-stitcher kept deliberately exhaustive wording and chose "recognized" over "consumed", which has a specific FOCUS meaning. shawnalpay approved on condition that Matt-Cowsert bring back the cut amortization sentence as a normative requirement in TF-3 work. Members approved it on 29 January 2026 and it merged.
summaries.1785: This was shawnalpay's action item to draft the Invoice Detail and Billing Period datasets. shawnalpay opened #1900 in January 2026 but kept the item open to finish TODO sections, after delays from Contract Commitment work. After reviews in TF-1 brought no outstanding feedback, shawnalpay closed it as complete in February 2026.
summaries.1793: Matt-Cowsert logged this action item in December 2025 to draft a PR for #958's commitment eligibility indicator, which Task Force 3 had agreed should be a JSON structure holding the provider's term and a FOCUS category such as spend-based or usage-based. It waited on input from cnharris10, then SanjnaSrivatsaVMware published the draft PR. It was closed in January 2026, with supported-feature content still to come.
summaries.1797: mike-finopsorg reported that the FOCUS 1.3 List Unit Price requirements included a rule that really applied to ListCost and was already stated there. shawnalpay objected to parking it under the 1.4 consistency review and said it was not errata either. The March 16, 2026 Maintainers call brought it into scope, with Matt-Cowsert writing a PR. It was implemented through #2067 in March 2026.
summaries.1800: flanakin's pull request (#1094) added a Dataset Completeness attribute, first called Scenario Completeness, requiring FOCUS datasets to include x_ custom columns for native columns that FOCUS does not cover. Matt-Cowsert pushed for entity-focused wording, shawnalpay objected to any aggregation or granularity requirements, and the requirements-model JSON was dropped at mike-finopsorg's request. pydi-aws asked for SHOULD instead of MUST, warning AWS exports would exceed 100 columns; mike-finopsorg called the omission clause an impossible bar, and shawnalpay proposed relying on column selection with a default column set. sarahcloudpm raised data-volume concerns. TF2 settled on including everything and documenting exclusions with justification. shawnalpay objected that flanakin's AI-assisted workflow recommitted suggestions separately, denying commenters co-authorship. Members approved it on March 26, 2026, and it merged that month.
summaries.1803: shawnalpay logged this action item in January 2026 to draft a PR extending the Contract Commitment dataset. The work became #1924, which left draft in early February 2026 after incorporating feedback. shawnalpay closed the item on February 11, 2026, once #1924 was stable, aiming for Member review by February 17.
summaries.1816: For #1091 and FOCUS 1.4, flanakin proposed a Dataset Configuration attribute requiring that a dataset can be limited to user-selected columns while still meeting column rules. Row aggregation, time granularity, version selection and row filtering went into supporting content as deferred ideas. Matt-Cowsert wanted that deferred material out of the PR; ijurica asked how conformance works when excluded columns are referenced by others, and flanakin softened the metadata rule to SHOULD after ijurica's feedback. mike-finopsorg had requirements-model files removed until 1.3 modelling finished, and jpradocueva said the rules described the dataset rather than an attribute. shawnalpay supplied rewrites and had it applied to Contract Commitment too. flanakin also reclassified unit price columns as dimensions and posted AI-generated update summaries. Members approved it in February 2026 and it was merged.
summaries.1865: For #1844, mike-finopsorg moved column presence requirements out of individual column files and into each dataset's definition. shawnalpay noted readers would lose the presence rule beside each column's feature level and suggested a Content Constraints entry naming and linking the dataset, which mike-finopsorg added to every column. ijurica proposed matching changes to the requirements guidelines and a rule order. Members approved it without objections in February 2026.
summaries.1878: shawnalpay opened this placeholder in January 2026 to collect work for the FOCUS 1.4 consistency review, scheduled for April 9 to 30, and triaged each reported inconsistency into an action item or pull request. shawnalpay's own items included a dedicated Allowed Values subsection (#2106), an invoice issuer glossary entry (#2107), an explicit JSON type requirement for Tags (#2114) and dataset ordering (#2120). ijurica flagged broken links, over-linking against the editorial guidelines and inconsistent references to participating entities. davidearney logged many editorial fixes, such as header capitalization, contractions, dash style and quoting of allowed values, and agreed to bundle them into one PR, #2200, with later fixes in #2203, #2204, #2205 and #2207. shawnalpay closed the task as complete in May 2026.
summaries.1880: jpradocueva opened this action item to automate extracting normative requirements from the spec's Markdown into JSON with at least 90% accuracy. jpradocueva found that lead-in statements such as "adheres to the following requirements" carried mandatory intent without BCP-14 keywords, and proposed explicit MUST wording; mike-finopsorg preferred "MUST adhere to the following requirements". After due-date delays, tracking moved in March 2026 to #2083, with the changes in #2090.
summaries.1882: Pull request #1882, by SanjnaSrivatsaVMware, added a Commitment Program Eligibility Details column listing the commitment programs a usage row is eligible for, to support coverage calculations (#1793, FR #958). The name kept changing: flanakin asked for a Details suffix like other JSON columns, rileyjenk said the scope was too narrow, TF-3 dropped 'Discount' to cover capacity reservations and SaaS commitments, and ijurica later suggested a full rename. Matt-Cowsert twice requested changes over type contradictions and redundant requirements; negotiated programs became optional and presence rules moved to dataset level. sarahcloudpm questioned the value of listing multiple programs. At shawnalpay's suggestion, separate lists became one CommitmentPrograms array, and shawnalpay warned it would be cut from 1.4 if unresolved by 9 April. Members approved it on 9 April 2026.
summaries.1888: shawnalpay proposed in January 2026 removing ProviderName and PublisherName, deprecated in 1.3, from the 1.4 specification, and documenting how removals are done. qquigley and TechinMama took on the work with help from davidearney, and the group agreed to generalise the removal process to all spec entities, not just columns. PR #1955 was approved and merged, and shawnalpay closed it as complete in March 2026.
summaries.1900: Pull request #1900, by shawnalpay, added two datasets, Invoice Detail for invoice reconciliation and Billing Period for billing cycle status, to support correction handling. rileyjenk asked about marketplace cases where both provider and invoice issuer produce invoice-like records. thecloudman argued an exchange rate column was vital; shawnalpay replied that TF-1 had not supported it, since a single invoice rate would create rounding errors against daily rates, and an effective rate can be derived. Matt-Cowsert suggested more invoice status values, but payment-related states had been ruled out of scope. ijurica wanted invoice-handling requirements from #1501 placed in these columns, and shawnalpay applied agreed changes such as making InvoiceId mandatory in Cost and Usage. Members approved it on 12 March 2026 and it merged.
summaries.1924: shawnalpay opened this PR to extend the Contract Commitment dataset with 17 columns covering commitment model, fulfilment and payment intervals, payment terms, discount and upfront percentages, lifecycle status, categories, currency and provider names, plus a JSON applicability column with its own schema and appendix scenarios. Review renamed several columns: Scope became Eligibility, then Applicability, after robmartin33 flagged overlap with FinOps Scopes, Interval became Fulfillment Interval, and Duration became Duration Type after rileyjenk's concern. ljadvey proposed dropping "Commitment" from the dataset name, which shawnalpay ruled out of scope because 1.3 had approved it. mike-finopsorg and Matt-Cowsert refined wording and constraints, and ijurica's late feedback removed Monetary Pool as a benefit category. Members approved it without objections on 12 March 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.1944: ijurica's action item was to draft a PR applying the normative requirements guidelines for attributes to the existing FOCUS attributes. ijurica posted draft #1967, still a work in progress, for TF-RM feedback. shawnalpay closed the item in February 2026, noting that #1981 was in draft.
summaries.1955: TechinMama's pull request removed the ProviderName and PublisherName columns deprecated in v1.3 (#1888), updating the dataset table, includes, changelog and migration guidance, and adding a column-removal process to the spec-change guidelines. TechinMama also fixed a CI failure caused by a deleted appendix file. Matt-Cowsert requested changes and pointed out two missed files. shawnalpay asked whether supporting-content files should be deleted, noting there was no precedent, and said the columns should be described as removed, not deprecated. davidearney questioned keeping references that would have to come out in v1.5. TF2 agreed to call spec components "entities" rather than "entries", aligning with #1960, and qquigley applied it. With six approvals, members approved it on February 26, 2026, and it merged.
summaries.1957: Matt-Cowsert logged this action item in February 2026 to use the term dataset instance where requirements meant concrete delivered data rather than the abstract FOCUS dataset. In April 2026 shawnalpay found the definition of done unclear, and ijurica pointed to a new convention making FOCUS Dataset the canonical normative subject. The scope was narrowed to four BilledCost and EffectiveCost requirements, and it was closed via #2269 in May 2026.
summaries.1966: Matt-Cowsert opened this pull request for #982 to rewrite the BilledCost and EffectiveCost requirements for 1.4, replacing marketplace and commitment-discount rules with a general covered and covering charge framework, new glossary terms and a rounding tolerance for invoice matching. beau-nelford-anglepoint called it a breaking change needing migration guidance; Matt-Cowsert replied that it clarified gaps in 1.3 rather than broke it. udam-stitcher argued a tolerance that grows with dataset size could mask real billing errors, while ijurica defended it as fixing a precision mismatch; maintainers reached no decision in March 2026, and Matt-Cowsert later added a formula co-authored with shawnalpay. Members approved it without objection on April 2, 2026, and it was merged that month.
summaries.1981: ijurica opened this pull request for #1059 to rewrite every attribute's normative requirements under the new guidelines in #1967: one subject and one BCP 14 keyword per requirement, a fixed set of subjects, and requirements moved to the dataset or column where they belong. It split ColumnHandling into FOCUS and custom column versions. Reviewers debated details: qquigley flagged conflicts with existing Id and Sku naming, thecloudman questioned rules on custom column abbreviations, which davidearney defended, and the requirements model team preferred singular subjects. A MAY-to-SHOULD change for alphabetical column order was agreed. On binding format rules to custom columns, shawnalpay set out options and mike-finopsorg's hybrid path was applied. Matt-Cowsert requested changes, then approved. Members approved it without objection on April 9, 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.1998: Issue #1998, opened by Matt-Cowsert in February 2026 under #982, was an action item to standardize the inconsistent use of 'match' and 'equal' in normative requirements, noticed while reviewing #1966. kk09v proposed 'equal' for numeric metric values and 'match' for everything else, and raised #2175. shawnalpay closed it in April 2026 as complete via the merged #2175.
summaries.2005: mike-finopsorg opened this action item in February 2026 to make the nested Object entity in JSON columns explicit in normative text, and raised #1986. shawnalpay reopened it after agreeing that mike-finopsorg would write a new pull request using JSON schema for presence and format requirements. Maintainers agreed on February 23 to proceed with #2007 over #1986, and the issue closed in favor of follow-up #2019.
summaries.2007: mike-finopsorg proposed replacing the lengthy normative text for JSON Object columns with formal JSON Schemas and moving inline examples to an appendix. After February 2026 maintainers discussion, shawnalpay closed the alternative #1986 in its favor, calling this approach easier to understand, implement and validate. kk09v requested changes on process grounds, since bundling the errata from #2041 broke the errata process, so shawnalpay moved those fixes to #2052. jpradocueva flagged uppercase MUST statements in implementation guidance, which mike-finopsorg considered non-normative. The new ContractCommitmentApplicability column moved to #1924, and mike-finopsorg decided to stay with JSON Schema for now under #2019. thecloudman warned that transferring requirements would need care. Members approved it on March 19, 2026, and it merged.
summaries.2015: jpradocueva made composite parent statements in normative requirements into explicit MUST statements, following #1880. shawnalpay raised consistency questions, such as varied sentence openings and whether conditional "when not null" composites should exist at all, and noted deprecated columns no longer needed changes. After approvals from thecloudman, shawnalpay and ijurica, Members approved it on March 5, 2026, and it was merged that month.
summaries.2016: ijurica logged this in February 2026 because ContractApplied required ContractCommitmentId to match ResourceId on all purchase charges, rather than only on purchases of that commitment and usage of its unused portion, as in DiscountHandling. shawnalpay would not add it to 1.4 without a Feature Request explaining the bug and another approval. ijurica created FR #2036, and in March 2026 the item was closed with PR #2017 in Member review.
summaries.2017: ijurica's pull request required ContractCommitmentId to equal ResourceId on purchases of that specific commitment and on usage of its unused portion, rather than on all purchases, matching Discount Handling. shawnalpay noted it needed a parent feature request for 1.4. udam-stitcher asked about credits and adjustments and noted the description overstated the change, which ijurica corrected. Members approved it on March 19, 2026, and it merged.
summaries.2018: Matt-Cowsert asked in February 2026 for FOCUS to show which AI model was used and to split input from output token costs, and shawnalpay strongly backed it for 1.5. DaveMoreau raised cached tokens, token units and inconsistent model names; kk09v raised context-window pricing, provisioned throughput and the risk of overloading properties. Task Force 2 proposed folding all AI scope into this request, but maintainers on May 11, 2026 kept it narrow, with topics such as #2371 and #2099 tracked separately. In June the group chose FOCUS-defined SkuPriceDetails properties over new columns, reused existing unit and quantity columns, and named the originator property Model Developer; ModelVariant was dropped in July. PR #2442 was merged by late July 2026, but the thread doesn't record the request's closure.
summaries.2047: jpradocueva's pull request (#2046) removed redundant "MUST be a valid decimal value" requirements, since the Decimal type and numeric format rules already covered them. shawnalpay and Matt-Cowsert requested changes after finding missed files, including pricingquantity.md, contractcommitmentcost.md and quantity columns using a "when not null" variant, which jpradocueva then fixed. Reviewers asked that supporting content be left alone and that the normative-requirements guidelines template be updated, where ijurica and Matt-Cowsert refined the placeholder syntax. shawnalpay asked whether "any valid decimal value" in content constraints was equally duplicative, and jpradocueva took that question to TF-RM. thecloudman and kk09v approved. Members approved it on March 26, 2026, and it merged the next day.
summaries.2052: shawnalpay's PR applied non-material errata to FOCUS 1.3 found while building validation tooling, including scoping contract presence rules to the ContractApplied Elements object, fixing JSON paths and a type, standardizing "Id" casing, correcting AllocatedTags, and bumping the requirements model to 1.3.0.1. kk09v, Matt-Cowsert and jpradocueva approved. Members approved it on March 19, 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2060: shawnalpay opened this PR to merge the 1.4 working draft into the candidate recommendation branch, keeping it in draft until late April 2026 to show the accumulating changes. mike-finopsorg set out how to resolve 15 merge conflicts left by 1.3 editorial work, and automated review findings were logged as non-blocking follow-ups such as #2145 and #2147. It was merged in May 2026, starting the 30-day IP review for 1.4.
summaries.2067: Matt-Cowsert removed requirements from ListUnitPrice and ContractedUnitPrice that restated rules already in ListCost and ContractedCost, following feedback in #1797. ijurica proposed also dropping a similar PricingQuantity requirement, which shawnalpay questioned, and that case was deferred to #2081; at shawnalpay's request, Requirements Model changes moved to #2049. Members approved it without objections on 26 March 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2085: davidearney reported a broken glossary link: effectivecost.md pointed to a hyphenated Charge Period anchor, while the glossary anchor had no hyphen. shawnalpay assigned it to consistency review. ijurica asked whether #2281 covered it, kk09v confirmed it did, and the issue was closed via #2281 in May 2026.
summaries.2086: davidearney reported that InvoiceIssuerName used present tense in the Invoice Detail dataset but past tense in the Billing Period dataset. shawnalpay agreed it belonged in the consistency review, and Task Force 3 agreed on April 10, 2026 to use present tense. It was completed by merged #2182 in April 2026.
summaries.2087: davidearney pointed out in March 2026 that the requirement that InvoiceIssuerName represent the invoicing entity appeared in two datasets but not in the Cost and Usage or Contract Commitment definitions. shawnalpay agreed it was a consistency issue and noted a wider pass was planned via #1890. It was completed by Matt-Cowsert's #2182, merged in April 2026.
summaries.2096: davidearney noted in March 2026 that Invoice Detail's ChargeCategory had a requirement allowing "Usage" for aggregated records that Cost and Usage lacked, and asked for a fix or explanation. shawnalpay said the difference was intentional and, at an April 2026 meeting, agreed to add a guideline allowing same-named columns to differ across datasets, with explanatory text. It was closed via #2295 in May 2026.
summaries.2097: davidearney reported that column files in the Invoice Detail and Billing Period datasets lacked the Dataset row that other datasets have in their Content Constraints tables. davidearney said #2200 fixed it, but shawnalpay reopened it in April 2026 because the row was still missing. It was closed in May 2026 via #2306.
summaries.2099: Matt-Cowsert asked in March 2026 for cached and uncached token costs to be distinguished; cache duration was later deferred. Task Force 2 voted in May to fold it into #2018, yet work continued here. In September a single TokenType property in #2606 became two, TokenCacheAction and TokenDirection, after flanakin argued for one attribute each. #2606 went to the October 1, 2026 members meeting; no comment records the outcome, and GitHub shows it closed as completed.
summaries.2100: Pull request #2100, by shawnalpay, made the InvoiceId and InvoiceDetailId feature levels Conditional, applying when the invoice issuer supports payable invoices, to match their requirements, and changed 'if' to 'when' across invoice-related datasets. shawnalpay acknowledged one change was not purely editorial, but ijurica judged it consistency rather than a material change. kk09v found the phrasing odd but not blocking. Members approved it on 2 April 2026.
summaries.2106: Issue #2106, opened by shawnalpay in March 2026, was an editorial task asking every column with a restricted value list to use a dedicated Allowed Values subheader, across four datasets. ijurica suggested placing it right below Requirements, and shawnalpay removed an incorrect link to #2200. davidearney's #2260 covered every item, and the issue closed in April 2026 as completed via that PR.
summaries.2112: kk09v added a Tag Scheme definition to the glossary, with links where the term was used, as a subset of the descoped #1904 (#1124). kk09v noted inconsistent use of provider-defined and data generator-defined and covered both in the definition, while shawnalpay and Matt-Cowsert suggested wording and grammar fixes. Members approved it without objection on April 2, 2026, and it was merged that month.
summaries.2113: Pull request #2113, by shawnalpay, applied the Dataset Configuration attribute from #1816 to the Invoice Detail and Billing Period datasets, which had not yet been approved via #1900 when that attribute was created. It was mechanical: ijurica, davidearney and Matt-Cowsert approved without issues, and Members approved it on 2 April 2026.
summaries.2128: shawnalpay reported that the editorial rule to link only the first occurrence of a column or attribute name was widely broken and unclear about what a "section" is. Maintainers agreed on once per source file, and shawnalpay proposed a glossary exception of once per entry. ijurica's #2312 defined the scope as the file and added exceptions for Content Constraints and the glossary. shawnalpay closed it via #2300 in May 2026.
summaries.2138: For #1389, shawnalpay finished moving column presence rules to the dataset level, covering three PricingCurrency columns whose composite presence requirements #1865 had not fully ported, and applied composite nullability to ContractCommitmentDiscountPercentage. jpradocueva confirmed the changes were valid under the requirements model extraction workflows. Members approved it without objections in April 2026.
summaries.2173: shawnalpay proposed small editorial fixes for AI #2110, such as mentioning PaaS beside SaaS, dropping unused normative keywords, alphabetising the appendix and removing a duplicate include. shawnalpay asked whether notes should follow the blockquote rule in AGENTS.md, and mike-finopsorg suggested keeping current practice and updating the guideline. Members approved it on April 16, 2026, and it was merged that day.
summaries.2175: kk09v proposed using "equal" for numeric metric values and "match" for identifiers and other values, and applied it across the spec for #1998. jpradocueva requested changes because the edits also altered the 1.2 and 1.3 requirements models, which kk09v reverted. Matt-Cowsert said the approach fitted the comparison guideline in #2236 and flagged one missed instance. Members approved it without objections in April 2026, when it merged.
summaries.2182: Matt-Cowsert's pull request (#2086) gave InvoiceIssuerName the same requirement in Billing Period, Invoice Detail, Contract Commitment and Cost and Usage, using present-tense "issues invoices" wording. shawnalpay pointed out that Contract Commitment also needed it, and it was added. TF3 floated tying the issuer to InvoiceId, assigning ijurica to draft wording; udam-stitcher liked the idea but did not require it. Members approved it on April 23, 2026, and it merged.
summaries.2200: Mostly editorial: davidearney applied 1.4 consistency fixes from #1878 across many files, covering heading capitalization, broken anchors, spacing and grammar, plus a workflow fix. Following shawnalpay and ijurica, double quotes were kept out of allowed-values tables; shawnalpay also said contractions could stay and dashes should be spaced hyphens. Matt-Cowsert noted the description no longer matched the diff. Members approved it without objections in April 2026.
summaries.2255: Matt-Cowsert pivoted two example tables in the PaymentCurrencyBilledCost column from horizontal to vertical, removing scaling wrappers added in #2038 that had shrunk the whole PDF. thecloudman approved but found the transposed layout hard to read and asked whether all examples would be made consistent; shawnalpay doubted that could be done in this round. Members approved it without objections on 16 April 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2258: thecloudman linked generic mentions of "invoice issuer" to its new glossary entry, which depended on #2257 adding that entry. shawnalpay asked for hyphenated anchors and, per a recent Maintainers agreement, a link only on the first mention in each file, noting the normative PR could go straight to approval because it only changed links. Members approved it without objections on 23 April 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2260: davidearney opened this pull request for #2106 to turn plain "Allowed values:" labels into proper Allowed Values headings placed directly after the Requirements section, in the 21 columns that define allowed values. This was an editorial change. shawnalpay asked davidearney to strip changes already made in #2200, such as header capitalization and anchor links, and to apply the move to every file; davidearney said the AI tool used had been told to skip #2200's changes, struck them by hand and rebased into one clean commit. shawnalpay asked whether moving the section would affect requirements extraction, and jpradocueva said it would not. An exception in one file was deferred to #2262. Members approved it without objection on April 23, 2026, and it was merged that month.
summaries.2262: davidearney asked whether ContractCommitmentDurationType should lose a lead-in sentence above its Allowed Values table, since #2106, via #2260, put such tables directly under the heading. shawnalpay kept it as an exception for now, noting the guidelines should cover such cases. In August 2026 davidearney reported it unchanged and suggested either recording a formal exception decision or removing the sentence. The thread doesn't record the outcome.
summaries.2269: ijurica added a guideline that requirements referring to datasets outside the subject position use precise glossary terms such as "dataset instance", and applied it across the spec. shawnalpay asked whether every case had been caught; ijurica described the regex scan used and later added one missed instance, and Matt-Cowsert noted circular guideline definitions were fixed. Members approved it without objections on 30 April 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2271: rileyjenk opened this pull request to make the spec's linter flag headers that broke the newly adopted Title Case rule. shawnalpay found bugs, such as acronyms and camelCase names being lowercased and hyphenated words being skipped, suggested exceptions such as is, are and vs., and proposed renaming "Introduced (version)" to "Version Introduced", which rileyjenk accepted. thecloudman reported false positives on On-Demand and Up-Front, which rileyjenk fixed. Because merging the rule alone would break the PDF build, shawnalpay held it until a companion PR applied the fixes; rileyjenk's #2302 was closed and shawnalpay's #2308 took its place. Members approved it without objection on April 30, 2026, and it was merged that month.
summaries.2274: kk09v's pull request (#2114) added a JSON data type requirement to key-value columns such as Tags, AllocatedTags and SkuPriceDetails. ijurica suggested wording that reads "JSON Object (serialized as a String where necessary)", and shawnalpay requested those changes. A review bot flagged the requirements model, which shawnalpay said would be handled separately. Members approved it on April 30, 2026, and it merged.
summaries.2275: ijurica's editorial PR, for #2127, fixed broken attribute links, used Attribute IDs in normative text, corrected the attributes overview table, and changed the MarkdownPP guidelines to say anchor generation keeps hyphens, matching the script. ijurica asked mike-finopsorg whether the regex was meant to strip hyphens; no reply is recorded. shawnalpay and jpradocueva approved, and Members approved it on April 23, 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2281: ijurica proposed fixing broken internal links outside the Attributes section, such as wrong paths, missing glossary anchors and case mismatches, for AI #2278. shawnalpay noted that FOCUS appeared in three different casings in anchors, and ijurica pointed to wider glossary anchor inconsistencies to handle separately. Members approved this editorial PR on April 30, 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2283: shawnalpay's editorial PR, for #2117, refactored the CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetails column to match other JSON object columns such as ContractApplied and AllocatedMethodDetails. It replaced the informal type definition with a formal JSON Schema, dropped structural requirements the schema now enforces, moved fictitious examples to an appendix, and used glossary terms in the intro. Matt-Cowsert requested changes twice, first for a duplicate bullet and a heading level, then for invalid JSON left after a Title Case suggestion from #2266 was applied, and approved once both were fixed. ijurica asked for "match" rather than "equal" in string comparisons and questioned whether the intro narrowed the scope; shawnalpay said no material change was intended and offered new wording. Members approved it on April 30, 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2284: ijurica's action item was to reword the AllocatedRatio sum requirement in AllocatedMethodDetails to follow the aggregate expression pattern in the normative requirements guidelines. shawnalpay closed it in April 2026, reopened it on finding #2285 was not yet merged, and closed it via #2285 in May 2026.
summaries.2285: ijurica's editorial PR reworded the AllocatedRatio sum requirement in AllocatedMethodDetails to the guidelines' "The sum of" and "be equal to" phrasing, matching #2175. shawnalpay confirmed at TF-1 that it followed kk09v's pattern, and jpradocueva approved it for the requirements model. Members approved it on 30 April 2026 and it merged.
summaries.2289: ijurica proposed renaming the Total Term value of ContractCommitmentFulfillmentInterval, because the glossary defines a term as an agreement rather than a duration, and scoping its description to the contract commitment. shawnalpay preferred Full Period to Full Commitment Period, asked for the rename to be applied everywhere and for merge conflicts to be resolved. Members approved it on April 30, 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2290: Editorial: for #2279, Matt-Cowsert applied a standard section order to column files, moving sections without changing content. shawnalpay argued JSON examples should directly follow the schema, and Matt-Cowsert swapped the order. flanakin asked about standardizing the varied names of extra sections; shawnalpay and ijurica said that belonged to #2108, with this PR a prerequisite. Members approved it without objections in April 2026.
summaries.2295: shawnalpay added a guideline allowing identically named columns to be defined differently across datasets, provided the spec explains why. The PR also restructured InvoiceDetail's ChargeCategory to fix overlapping MAY and MUST rules, explaining that invoice lines may aggregate charge types while Tax stays separate. ijurica offered non-blocking wording suggestions, and the section was renamed Implementation Guidance per #2310. Members approved it on 30 April 2026 and it merged.
summaries.2300: Editorial: deejacruz removed repeat links to the same anchor within column files for #2128, keeping only the first, across 46 files. shawnalpay asked whether once per file was too strict, and the April 23 Members' call exempted links in markdown tables, tracked as #2305. jpradocueva flagged one leftover charge period link. Members approved it without objections on April 30, 2026, when it merged.
summaries.2303: Matt-Cowsert added an editorial rule to use semicolons in lists whose items contain commas, for #2297, and applied it to eight passages. shawnalpay found further instances, and kk09v argued one case was two separate clauses, which shawnalpay accepted; kk09v also noted an em dash suited one clause. Members approved it without objections on April 30, 2026, when it merged.
summaries.2306: davidearney added the missing Dataset row to the Content Constraints tables of 29 column files, closing #2097. davidearney asked whether that cell should be an anchor link or plain text, and ijurica pointed out a Cost and Usage file also missing the row, which was then added. Members approved this editorial PR on April 30, 2026, and it was merged; the thread doesn't record an answer on links.
summaries.2310: ijurica proposed restructuring column headings for AI #2309, merging Implementation Context into Implementation Guidance and regrouping JSON object headings. shawnalpay opposed placing other headings between the column and object requirements, and mike-finopsorg said major structural changes came too late. Nesting all object sections under one object heading resolved the concern. Members approved it on April 30, 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2315: Matt-Cowsert opened this request after community feedback that the spec gave too little guidance on producing and querying split cost allocation data. thecloudman added an AllocatedServiceName column in #2395, merged by August 2026, with follow-ups #2493 and #2494, and #2655 refined its requirements. TF-2 argued at length over what an unallocated portion row should carry, and dropped that requirement in September 2026. No comment records the outcome; GitHub shows it closed as completed.
summaries.2321: ijurica proposed fixing remaining Content Constraints inconsistencies across all four datasets for AI #2320, such as column types and value format casing. shawnalpay and davidearney asked for matching dataset.md updates and consistent Allowed values casing, and Matt-Cowsert filed #2326 for a link text convention. Members approved this editorial PR on April 30, 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2325: Matt-Cowsert asked that tag keys, like tag values, be preserved as provided, after #2322 reported mixed-case versions of one key in Azure exports. #2434 carried the change: TF-2 adopted "provided keys" wording, moved a section on platform key handling to supporting content and cut a sentence contradicting the case-sensitive requirement. In July 2026 the PR went to member approval. No comment records the outcome; GitHub shows it closed as completed.
summaries.2340: ijurica's pull request fixed six internal links in JSON Object Format columns broken by the 1.4 heading restructuring, plus two schema anchors with an extra path segment. Matt-Cowsert checked all eight targets and confirmed no other files had the broken anchors. The change was editorial; members approved it on May 7, 2026, and it merged.
summaries.2344: ijurica opened this PR to fix a subset of normative wording inconsistencies found in the 1.4 review (#2334), such as replacing actor-based subjects like "data generator" with state-based wording, swapping "if" for "when" and splitting multi-part requirements, with most metadata changes deferred. shawnalpay and ijurica reworked BillingPeriodStatus and InvoiceIssueStatus into parallel previous-status phrasing, and agreed to leave some process verbs in dataset completeness for now. kk09v warned that removing the data generator from a Tags requirement changed its meaning, and questioned verbs in SkuPriceId. Matt-Cowsert restored dropped links. jpradocueva noted the IP review period and said the Tags and delivery handling changes bordered on non-editorial, acceptable only with unanimous agreement. Members approved it without objections on May 7, 2026, and it merged in May 2026.
summaries.2349: shawnalpay's PR moved the rules for when each dataset must be present out of the individual dataset files into one section of data_model.md, with minor phrasing cleanups. jpradocueva first requested changes because the file lacked the entity type and sections the requirements model needs, then approved. After normative edits, approvals were reset under the 1.5 practice and Matt-Cowsert re-approved. Members approved it on May 14, 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2351: shawnalpay opened this PR to replace inline conditional wording such as "when the service provider supports X" with 25 formal, verifiable Condition files, linked from the dataset tables, plus an Operating Model glossary term in place of mixed references to providers and generators. After feedback shawnalpay shortened the terms to "Operating model" and "Condition". ijurica suggested consistent Includes or Supports names, a capability-centred Operating Model definition, and letting providers expose a value when only one exists, which shawnalpay partly deferred to #2375. A Baseline condition was struck to be proposed separately, and ContractedCost and ChargeFrequency changes moved to #2374 and #2375. Matt-Cowsert requested editorial fixes, and jpradocueva noted requirements-model assumptions needing validation. Members approved it without objections on May 28, 2026, and it merged in May 2026.
summaries.2358: shawnalpay opened this in May 2026 to add actor columns for attributing SaaS and GenAI spend, separating the system actor from the end consumer while avoiding personal data. After Matt-Cowsert noted that marketplaces and relay services record different identity layers, #2360 proposed PrincipalId and ConsumerId. TF-2 debated nullability, an opt-in for high-cardinality columns (#2473, later moved to 1.6) and whether "Principal" sounded too legal, keeping the name. In June 2026 the group decided PrincipalId would ship first and made ConsumerId a carve-out (#2495). Richer identity data went to #2553 as CredentialId and RequesterDetails, which udam-stitcher restructured as a JSON array despite shawnalpay questioning that shape. By September 30, 2026 both #2360 and #2553 had merged, while #2473 stayed open for 1.6.
summaries.2360: shawnalpay proposed a PrincipalId column identifying the identity and access principal behind a charge, first paired with a ConsumerId column. ijurica pushed to align terminology and link the work to the broader AI attribution request #2018, and reviewers debated authenticated versus authorized, nullability and plain-text PII. Matt-Cowsert took over the PR in June 2026 while shawnalpay was away; ConsumerId moved to draft #2495 and a delivery grain idea was deferred. When udam-stitcher proposed a richer Principal object with names and emails, Maintainers decided in July 2026 to keep one IAM-based identifier, with details in a companion column on #2553. flanakin questioned what the IncludesPrincipals condition meant, and the final version keyed presence on requester attribution. Members approved it without objections on 10 September 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2377: Issue #2377, opened by shawnalpay in May 2026, proposed new Service Category values and cloud-neutral descriptions so on-premises, SaaS and licensing costs need not default to Other. ThavronNan took it over, and TF-1 split it into cleanup (#2379) and expansion (#2518) PRs, the expansion moving toward 1.6. By August 2026 the remaining scope was #2624, fixing the Compute description and splitting out Bare Metal. No comment records the outcome; GitHub shows it closed as completed.
summaries.2379: shawnalpay opened this PR, under #2377, to make Service Category apply beyond cloud. Early drafts added values such as Hardware, Software Licensing, Telecommunications and Facilities; Matt-Cowsert and mike-finopsorg argued Hardware overlapped Compute, Storage and Networking, so it was struck, and flanakin asked whether licenses and support belong in the category they serve. shawnalpay assigned the PR to ThavronNan during a leave. In July 2026 Task Force 1 split it (#2504): Matt-Cowsert re-scoped this PR to rewording five cloud-specific descriptions and reordering Multicloud, with no value changes, and moved the expansion to #2518. After approvals from Matt-Cowsert, davidearney and jpradocueva, Members approved it on July 23, 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2395: thecloudman proposed an AllocatedServiceName column because split cost allocation rules keep the origin ServiceName on allocated rows, so the consuming service, such as EKS running on EC2, could not be queried by name. ijurica found older gaps in the split cost allocation attribute, which thecloudman moved to #2515, and the appendix queries and requirements model rules were pulled out, the latter to #2554. Asked whether the need was AWS-specific, thecloudman found the service swap pattern was but argued for a FOCUS column anyway. flanakin approved while calling the whole Allocated column pattern tech debt. A requirement tying values to existing ServiceName values, raised by flanakin and kk09v, went to a follow-on PR by kk09v. Members approved it on 6 August 2026, and it was merged that month.
summaries.2396: thecloudman opened an action item, for #2315, to draft columns naming the consuming service on split cost allocation rows while keeping the original service intact. shawnalpay repeatedly asked for a due date and removed it from the 1.5 milestone until a Maintainer approved a PR. In July 2026 Matt-Cowsert reported it complete, with the scope cut to AllocatedServiceName and AllocatedServiceCategory dropped.
summaries.2412: shawnalpay opened this action item to propose revisions to the Service Categories in #2379. ThavronNan shared spreadsheets of category and subcategory recommendations covering on-premises spend, discussed over several June 2026 Task Force 1 meetings, and davidearney proposed AI and Machine Learning description fixes and new Generative AI subcategories. Matt-Cowsert closed it in July 2026, since the expansion was tracked in #2518 and #2379 was in member review.
summaries.2424: Pull request #2424, by shawnalpay, added a SKU Price dataset for rate cards, negotiated prices and quantity tiers (#2364); Matt-Cowsert carried it during shawnalpay's leave from June 2026. TF-1 chose a current-snapshot model, renamed volume tiers to quantity tiers, dropped ChargeFrequency and kept commitment-discount signals out of prices. The price structure swung: UnitPriceCategory rows, then separate list and contracted price columns, then in September a single unit price column so each price keeps its own dates. deejacruz proposed extending UnitPriceCategory, and thecloudman flagged reused column IDs with different nullability. In October shawnalpay accepted making SkuPriceId tier-unique despite adoption concerns. flanakin's sustained objection at the 8 October Members meeting was met by #2752 marking the dataset as preview, and Members approved it on 29 October 2026.
summaries.2432: ijurica corrected the Cost and Usage overview table, which said HostProviderName did not allow nulls, contradicting the column's own constraints and requirements. Matt-Cowsert confirmed the fix matched the column definition, and jpradocueva noted it did not affect the Requirements Model. Members approved it without objections on 4 June 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2434: Pull request #2434, by thecloudman, restored a requirement, dropped in #691, that user-defined tag keys match the keys provided, after feedback (#2322) that Azure exports showed one key in several casings. Maintainers framed it as fidelity to user input, not normalization. flanakin and thecloudman flagged that 'at the source' clashed with the Tag Source glossary term, so Matt-Cowsert's 'provided keys' wording was adopted; flanakin's worry that the prefix exception left prefixed keys unconstrained was also fixed. ijurica asked to revert requirements-model file changes as out of scope, and TF-2 moved the key-casing explanation into supporting content. jpradocueva's question about the normative subject was deferred to AI #2535. Members approved it on 6 August 2026.
summaries.2441: Matt-Cowsert noted during review of #2390 that dataset overview tables linked each conditional column to a single condition, even when presence depended on several, and asked for a convention. Task force updates in August 2026 recorded that ijurica's #2625 would instead drop those links, relying on a planned conditions row in each column's constraints table. No comment records the outcome; GitHub shows it closed as completed.
summaries.2442: Matt-Cowsert's pull request (#2018) added AI model identity as FOCUS-defined SkuPriceDetails properties, not new columns, with an appendix example. shawnalpay asked why it used "Model" rather than the more general "Product"; Matt-Cowsert argued FOCUS had already retired a general producer column, PublisherName, and TF2 kept Model in June 2026. For the maker key, ModelProvider and ModelAuthor were set aside as too close to the deprecated Provider and Publisher terms, and Matt-Cowsert chose ModelDeveloper, which thecloudman backed with an app store analogy. davidearney questioned ModelId differing between sellers, so its description was clarified as seller-namespaced. TF2 dropped ModelVariant in July 2026 because market naming was unsettled. Members approved it on July 16, 2026, and it merged that month.
summaries.2492: ijurica opened this feature request in June 2026 listing gaps in ListCost, ListUnitPrice, ContractedCost and ContractedUnitPrice, such as unclear discount boundaries and no rule on which pricing tier to report. Matt-Cowsert's TF1 updates tracked tiered-pricing glossary terms (#2564) and revised definitions (#2567, #2690), with IncludesUnitPricing kept for v1.5. In November 2026 #2564 was still unmerged and ijurica opened #2839. The thread doesn't record the final outcome.
summaries.2510: Pull request #2510, by mike-finopsorg, was repository maintenance adding a pytest stage to the spec build that checks JSON blocks, JSON schemas, internal links and SQL examples, and fixing broken links the tests found. Matt-Cowsert ran the suite, confirmed it passed after automated review findings were addressed, and noted the description understated the test files. Members approved it on 30 July 2026.
summaries.2549: For #2530, Matt-Cowsert replaced a compound SHOULD bullet in ContractCommitmentDurationType with one format requirement, leaving quantity and unit detail to the Expected Format section; the matching fix for PurchaseDurationType was in #2424. kk09v wanted the time units linked to Unit Format and questioned Quarter; Matt-Cowsert kept them separate, adding a note, and sent the Quarter question to #2600. Members approved it in August 2026.
summaries.2550: Matt-Cowsert, assigned with ijurica, reviewed virtual currency wording, since "tokens" now also meant an AI unit and "credits" clashed with the Credit charge category. In August 2026 Matt-Cowsert found CurrencyFormat contradicted itself, allowing virtual currency yet requiring ISO 4217 codes, and recommended narrowing the allowance to consumption currency and keeping cryptocurrency out, in draft #2617. The item closed that month, with tracking moved to the PR.
summaries.2553: Matt-Cowsert opened this PR to add CredentialId and a JSON RequesterDetails column to Cost and Usage, completing the three-column requester model Maintainers settled on 3 August 2026 alongside PrincipalId from #2360. The details column was renamed several times before becoming RequesterDetails. flanakin pressed for explicit PII warnings, but TF-2 kept a single dataset-level note. udam-stitcher doubted a free-form object would work; Matt-Cowsert pointed to its strict published schema and applied most of udam-stitcher's wording changes. TF-2 ruled that RequesterDetails must not be null when either identifier is present, and the wider question of when details columns may be null went to #2718. The PR also revised PrincipalId nullability. Members approved it without objections on 24 September 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2562: Issue #2562, opened by ijurica in July 2026, was an action item to extract the agreed description changes for ListCost, ContractedCost, ListUnitPrice and ContractedUnitPrice from staging PR #2513 into a dedicated PR for FR #2492. ijurica published the draft on 28 July, extended the deadline and added a requirement for alignment with another contributor. On 4 August 2026 ijurica reported the PR issued, alignment reached and the task complete.
summaries.2567: ijurica proposed revising ListUnitPrice, ContractedUnitPrice, ListCost and ContractedCost: removing two operating model conditions, calling List pricing service-provider-suggested rather than published, and separating negotiated pricing terms, reflected in Contracted metrics, from commitment discount effects, reflected in neither. The scope grew to SKU and pricing currency columns. Proposed glossary terms for unit price adjustments and post-pricing discounts were dropped after the August 10, 2026 maintainers meeting. Matt-Cowsert and jpradocueva flagged conflicting rules on credit rows, and Task Force 1 kept an unqualified rule that cost columns match for Tax and Credit charges. marc-perreaut questioned terms such as service-provider-suggested, flanakin proposed simpler wording, and udam-stitcher felt the aligned usage sentences undersold Billed and Effective Cost; ijurica kept most wording. The group agreed it on October 8, 2026, and it merged the next day.
summaries.2579: ijurica's pull request (#2130) removed a cost-formula requirement from PricingQuantity that duplicated ListCost and ContractedCost, following the approach of #2067. Matt-Cowsert noted that #1967 had since written this don't-repeat-yourself rule into the contributor guidelines, and jpradocueva and thecloudman also approved. Members approved it without objection on August 13, 2026, and it merged.
summaries.2580: jpradocueva's pull request (#2425) began filling the Conditions row of Content Constraints tables, giving three template examples: no condition ("Not applicable"), one condition, and several. ijurica suggested dropping "Recommended when" because the feature level already says so, and kk09v agreed. flanakin asked about "None" versus "Not applicable" and how multi-row conditions render in the PDF. Members approved it on September 3, 2026, and it merged.
summaries.2600: flanakin proposed, for FR #2709, requiring ContractCommitmentDurationType to use the largest whole time unit, so 12 Months becomes 1 Year and providers group consistently. Matt-Cowsert noted that with Quarter allowed, the spec's own 3 Months examples would break; Task Force 1 dropped Quarter on September 1, 2026, accepting flanakin's view that it implies calendar or fiscal alignment, and adopted UnitFormat's time units. After kk09v asked about UnitFormat, Week and a general largest-unit SHOULD were added there. shawnalpay asked for the MUST to be scoped so it did not override the existing SHOULDs. rileyjenk wished for ISO 8601 durations, which flanakin called a breaking change worth revisiting for 2.0. A SKU consistency case moved to #2424. The group agreed it on October 1, 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2606: Matt-Cowsert's pull request (#2099) separated cached from uncached AI token costs using SkuPriceDetails properties, following #2442. In September 2026 TF2 replaced the single TokenType property with TokenCacheAction and TokenDirection, the first FOCUS-defined properties with allowed values; iwasinnam2 backed the token-specific names. flanakin asked that output rows and SKUs without caching not carry the cache property, which was adopted. thecloudman questioned a composite scenario, and ijurica and jpradocueva criticized a cache cost efficiency query, which was removed. Token, AI Model and Prompt Cache glossary entries were added. shawnalpay requested simpler wording for prose that seemed AI-generated, and many suggestions were applied. The group agreed to it on October 1, 2026, and it merged October 2.
summaries.2617: Matt-Cowsert opened this PR to fix a contradiction in the CurrencyFormat attribute, which allowed virtual currency but required ISO 4217 codes for every value, a leftover from the 1.4 refactor. The fix required ISO codes only for national currencies, barred them otherwise, and limited PricingCurrency to national or consumption currencies, keeping cryptocurrency out. shawnalpay asked that examples avoid the word "token", reserved for a unit of measure, so the sample currency became OmniBucks. ijurica flagged circular wording in the conditions, which was reworked, and Matt-Cowsert concluded that UnitFormat's token references could stay. TF-1 agreed in September 2026 to rename the IncludesVirtualCurrency condition to IncludesConsumptionCurrency here. The group agreed the PR on 1 October 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2624: ijurica proposed adding physical compute to the Compute category and splitting the Virtual Machines subcategory into Bare Metal and Virtual Machines, depending on whether a provider-managed hypervisor is present. Matt-Cowsert noted that dedicated hosts fit neither row, so ijurica kept wording placing them under Virtual Machines, and shawnalpay had "high-performance" dropped. thecloudman approved but noted the requirements model lacked Bare Metal. Members approved it in September 2026 and it merged.
summaries.2625: This editorial PR by ijurica removed repeated condition links from the dataset files, keeping one per condition, and dropped condition links from overview table cells because multi-condition columns linked only one (#2441). Matt-Cowsert noted column files did not yet state their conditions, which ijurica said #2580 addressed; the PR was retargeted to stand alone rather than depend on #2567. Members approved it on 3 September 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2640: Matt-Cowsert opened this for #2614 because seven of ten SkuPriceId values in the commitment discount example data each named several price points. It split them into 24 single-price-point identifiers, aligned rates, and added granularity guidance plus two new Cost and Usage SkuPriceId requirements. flanakin approved but saw one requirement as duplicating the SKU Price key; Matt-Cowsert replied they constrained different things. It was approved and merged in September 2026.
summaries.2655: kk09v proposed, for FR #2315 and replacing #2612, making AllocatedServiceName follow AllocatedMethodId for nullability, so the unallocated portion of a split carries a value, and adding a SHOULD to match the generator's ServiceName. kk09v compared how AWS and GCP report unallocated Kubernetes costs. ijurica questioned which value the unallocated row should take, thecloudman proposed a carve-out for multi-service splits, and shawnalpay queried the phrase "independently billed". Matt-Cowsert and thecloudman noted the rule also reached retained origin rows, left open in #2515. On September 30, 2026 Task Force 2 removed a MUST about the unallocated row after ijurica showed it could never fail; it may return in 1.6. beau-finopsorg queried the removal. The group agreed the PR on October 1, 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2719: This mechanical PR by jpradocueva reapplied the condition link removals from #2625, which #2580 had undone by merging later the same day. Only link markup changed. Matt-Cowsert approved, supplied missing description text, resolved a conflict with #2553, and urged merging before other PRs touching the same files. It was merged in September 2026.
summaries.2752: flanakin opened this pull request, stacked on #2595 and #2424, to mark the SKU Price dataset, its examples and dependent features as a preview in FOCUS 1.5, using non-normative notes and a "(preview)" label without changing requirements. ijurica approved, wanting new datasets released as previews by default, as Cost and Usage had been in 1.0 Preview, and thecloudman also supported it. shawnalpay objected that nothing should be marked preview until FOCUS publicly defined what preview means and how content enters and leaves it, and said they would abstain; #2762 set out that guidance. Matt-Cowsert asked for notes stating what the preview excluded from conformance, which flanakin added, while ijurica's glossary links were deferred. Members approved it with one abstention on October 29, 2026, and it was merged that month.
summaries.2757: finops-DaveMoreau made an editorial fix, capitalizing Display Name references in four column introductions, such as Availability Zone and Billing Currency, closing #2740 and following #2567. Three fixes came from a lint rule proposed in #2759, and Sub Account Name was found on review. ijurica approved and suggested follow-up work on other Display Name cases. Members approved it without objection on October 22, 2026, and it was merged that month.
summaries.2773: ijurica aligned references and links across 59 files with the editorial, normative requirements and MarkdownPP guidelines for #2772, leaving unclear cases unchanged and listed. Matt-Cowsert caught a new link sending "term" to the wrong glossary entry, which ijurica dropped, and ijurica declined flanakin's hyphenation suggestion. thecloudman noted the 1.5 requirements model still held old wording. Members approved it without objections on October 29, 2026, when it merged.
summaries.2788: flanakin's AI-drafted editorial PR changed the Operating Model Conditions label to sentence case in all 127 column files, closing #2715. Matt-Cowsert listed other open PRs needing the same edit, and ijurica flagged casing differences in other tables for 1.6. Members approved it on 29 October 2026 and it merged.
summaries.2789: Editorial: in an AI-drafted PR for #2703, flanakin removed a repeated schema link from the example pointers of five JSON columns instead of adding an exception to the first-occurrence linking rule. Matt-Cowsert logged action items to take it out of draft before the 1.5 consistency review closed and to fix its issue-closing keyword. Members approved it without objections in October 2026.
summaries.2791: Matt-Cowsert converted note callouts across the specification to the blockquote format in the editorial guidelines, resolving #2528 and leaving disclaimers to #2775. udam-stitcher asked whether SKU Price Details footnotes needed both a bullet and a superscript, so they became a numbered list, and rileyjenk suggested adding the rule to the linter. Members approved this editorial PR on October 29, 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.2802: Matt-Cowsert's PR renamed RequesterDetailsValue to RequesterDetailsObject and nested its entry requirements so the requirements model extractor would capture them, after the gap was raised on #2710; no requirement wording changed. davidearney and jpradocueva approved, and ijurica noted that Entry is undefined in the spec. Members approved it on 29 October 2026 and it merged.
